name: Ted Cruz
subject: History was made this week...
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Ted Cruz for Senate
body:
| | | | _**FROM THE DESK OF SENATOR TED CRUZ **_
---
| | | Fellow Conservative,
---
History was made this week...

For months, we were saying that 2026 was the most consequential midterm election of our lifetimes.

Unfortunately, we were right. Sometimes history is to be celebrated; other times, it is to be mourned. Always, it must be reckoned with.

2026 was not simply a blue wave; it was a blue tsunami. It was an ass kicking. It was not simply a bad 2006 midterm election. It was a Watergate-level repudiation. What happened, and why? What are the consequences, and where on earth do we go from here?

When all the votes were counted, the problem wasn't turnout. Instead, our voters, Republicans, Libertarians, Independents, showed up and voted, and rejected our candidates, voting Democrat instead. We've lost the House. We've lost the Senate. When all is said and done, we will have lost eight to 10 Senate seats.

We lost in historically red states, like South Carolina and North Carolina, Kansas and Iowa. We lost in purple states, like Michigan, and New Hampshire, and Georgia. And we just barely won by just a single point in bright red states like Florida and Louisiana, and then there's Texas.

Nowhere are the consequences of this election greater than Texas. In the Lone Star State, we lost every single statewide election. For weeks, I had been publicly warning on this podcast that we were in very real danger of losing everything in Texas. Far too few believed that was possible. I am very, very sorry that it came to pass. Texas has not had a Democrat governor since 1994. We haven't had a Democrat senator since 1993. Now we'll have both.

Why were the results so overwhelming? Pundits and analysts will break down the results for weeks or months or even years to come, but several things are already evident today.

Years ago, the very best political advice I ever got was from Heidi. She said, "It's not about you. It's about them. It's about their kids, their families, their hopes, their dreams, their futures." Too many politicians forget that.

Take the state of Kansas, for example, a state that has not elected a Democrat senator since 1932. It just did. Here's what exit polling showed were the top issues in Kansas.

Number one, cost of living, energy, and groceries. That was listed as number one by 30.6 percent of voters.
Corruption. Number two, 18.5%.
The cost of the Iran war, 10.1%.
The candidates are terrible, 7.9%.
The Canada trade war, 7.6%.
The GOP didn't do enough to support Trump, 6.6%.
Republicans didn't pass the Save America Act, 5.6%.
Trump's focus on monuments, 5.5%, and data centers and AI, 3.8%...

The top issue, cost of living, is very real. Too many in politics dismissed it. They didn't understand. They pointed to the macro numbers showing the stock markets soaring, median income at record highs, and poverty at record lows. Those data are true, but they don't tell all of the story.

Here are some stats that are a lot more real and personal. Spam, Hormel's processed meat substitute, broke record sales, selling 113 million cans last year. That is nearly as much spam as was sold during the entirety of World War II. 29 percent of Americans have used buy now, pay later for groceries this year. That's double the share just two years ago.

In August, banks repossessed 42% more homes than they did last year. In 2024, car repossessions topped 2.3 million, above the 2009 peak in the middle of the Great Financial Crisis. In 2025, 6% of 401k holders took hardship withdrawals, paying penalties. That is a record, and triple the norm.

And here's one that's really stunning. Americans made more than 75 million paid plasma donations in 2026. That's another record. That means 200,000 Americans every single day, with a needle in their arm, just to pay for groceries.

That is very real pain from real Americans, and too many Republican politicians seem like they didn't understand or they didn't care. Food is too high, gas is too high, diesel is too high, insurance is too high, life is too high.

Tariffs have made everything too expensive, and the Iran war has dragged on too long. It should have been brief, decisive, and over. It needs to end, and we should never, under any circumstances, give the Ayatollah billions of dollars.

There's a very real economic disconnect. Our K-shaped economy is a yawning divide. Last year, we saw the world's very first trillionaire, a modern-day Thomas Edison, at the very same time that millions were struggling to feed their families. Data centers being constructed were turning billionaires into centibillionaires, while simultaneously the average American's electricity bill went up 30% in the last five years.

Understandably, people were pissed off, and elected Republicans didn't do enough to address their very real pain.

So, what do we do now? We need to listen and respond. We need to champion economic policies that make a real difference in working people's lives, and we need to deal with the consequences.

Texas is blue. That is a hard sentence to utter. But Texas, today at least, is blue. As we sit here today, I am the only statewide elected Republican who remains in Texas. That's not something I ever thought I would say.

We can be certain that the Democrats in Austin and in Washington will overshoot. In Texas, they will try to raise taxes dramatically. They may even try to adopt a state income tax, or even a California wealth tax. They will try to shut down the energy industry, destroying jobs across our state. They will embrace the radical transgender agenda. They will persecute those they perceive to be enemies, especially Elon Musk.

And in Washington, they will attack Trump every single day, constantly. Impeachment hearings, subpoenas, his family, cabinet members, business leaders, open persecution, and nonstop retaliation. Make no mistake. Nationally, the radicals are in charge. The communists and the Islamists who have taken over the Democrat Party have now taken over the United States Congress. They will be unleashed.

Sadly, that means many Americans will be hurt. Texans will be hurt. Their assault on business will make Texas a much less attractive place to start or grow a small business. Texas will become more like California if they succeed in halting all new investment into AI.

The economic results will be dramatic. Over $700 billion in new projects are scheduled to start in the next year. If the Democrats shut them all down, our country will very likely go into a recession. That will suit the Democrats just fine. They'll just blame it all on Donald Trump.

In the next two years, we need to do two things.

One, fight the madness. I will work with Democrats when they're willing to be reasonable. Last night, I called James Talarico. I congratulated him on his very impressive victory. It was a pleasant conversation, and I told him that I looked forward to working with him to try to benefit Texas.

So, if there are things like flood relief for the Hill Country, or trying to get the space academy to Texas, he and I will work together. But if the newly elected radicals push policies that hurt Texas, raising taxes, destroying jobs, opening the border, releasing violent criminals, threatening our children, undermining our constitutional rights, I will fight with all of my strength to defend Texas and to defend the Constitution.

And number two, we need to rebuild, getting behind policies that directly benefit the constituents we lost.

There's a complicated story, no doubt, of what happened on Election Day, but as I see it, the key constituencies we lost were blue-collar voters, what had rightly become the core base of our party, Evangelical Christians, who didn't show up with the same numbers and fervor as prior elections, farmers and ranchers. Tragically, we alienated rural America. Young people, who excitedly had voted Republican in 2024, and who shifted hard blue this cycle. And of course, Hispanics.

For Hispanics, there's a strong overlap with young people and blue-collar workers. In 2024, just two years ago, I was proud to carry Hispanics statewide in Texas by six points, and we swung the Rio Grande Valley red for the first time in a century. It can be done, but in this election, those Hispanic voters overwhelmingly went back Democrat. We have got to turn that around.

And for young people, we need to be the party of the future. We need to champion policies that expand their future. Our two single biggest legislative accomplishments of the past two years, Trump Accounts and the school choice tax credit, which will unleash tens of billions of dollars in new scholarships for kids, are generationally powerful. I was proud to author both of those transformational policies, and yet too few candidates all across the country ran on that record.

Too few voters were even aware of what we'd accomplished for their kids and their future. But we need to build. We need to expand to continue creating a new investor class for hundreds of millions of Americans, help everyone, every American, become an owner, to have real skin in the game, to create new generations of capitalists ready to reject socialism.

People voted as they did because they were angry. Ironically, the Democrats that they elected are going to advance policies that will make affordability worse. The Democrats want gas prices higher. They want to ban gasoline engines altogether. Their extreme environmental mandates will drive up food prices and the prices of everything else.

But hear me now: we will bring Texas back. I am filled with hope and optimism. Texas will be red again. We have not suddenly become a bunch of tofu-eating, gun-banning, tutu-wearing pinko commie liberals. That ain't us. Texas is still Texas.

We will rebuild as a true blue-collar party, not by embracing socialism, but by being real free-market conservatives. The way we built the Texas economic miracle in the first place, and we will build and rebuild America as well.

When the zealots overreach, and they will, we will stand ready to lead in the direction of freedom, of prosperity, of safety, and security, and common sense. We will return to a new dawn of freedom in America.

It is dark right now, but it is always darkest before the dawn, and morning is coming. That is my fervent prayer, and that is my commitment to you.
---
Thank you,
---
---
Ted Cruz

Spam, Hormel's processed meat substitute, broke record sales, selling 113 million cans last year. That is nearly as much spam as was sold during the entirety of World War II. 29 percent of Americans have used buy now, pay later for groceries this year. That's double the share just two years ago. In August, banks repossessed 42% more homes than they did last year. In 2024, car repossessions topped 2.3 million, above the 2009 peak in the middle of the Great Financial Crisis. In 2025, 6% of 401k holders took hardship withdrawals, paying penalties. That is a record, and triple the norm. And here's one that's really stunning. Americans made more than 75 million paid plasma donations in 2026. That's another record. That means 200,000 Americans every single day, with a needle in their arm, just to pay for groceries. That is very real pain from real Americans, and too many Republican politicians seem like they didn't understand or they didn't care. Food is too high, gas is too high, diesel is too high, insurance is too high, life is too high. Tariffs have made everything too expensive, and the Iran war has dragged on too long. It should have been brief, decisive, and over. It needs to end, and we should never, under any circumstances, give the Ayatollah billions of dollars. There's a very real economic disconnect. Our K-shaped economy is a yawning divide. Last year, we saw the world's very first trillionaire, a modern-day Thomas Edison, at the very same time that millions were struggling to feed their families. Data centers being constructed were turning billionaires into centibillionaires, while simultaneously the average American's electricity bill went up 30% in the last five years. Understandably, people were pissed off, and elected Republicans didn't do enough to address their very real pain. So, what do we do now? We need to listen and respond. We need to champion economic policies that make a real difference in working people's lives, and we need to deal with the consequences. Texas is blue. That is a hard sentence to utter. But Texas, today at least, is blue. As we sit here today, I am the only statewide elected Republican who remains in Texas. That's not something I ever thought I would say. We can be certain that the Democrats in Austin and in Washington will overshoot. In Texas, they will try to raise taxes dramatically. They may even try to adopt a state income tax, or even a California wealth tax. They will try to shut down the energy industry, destroying jobs across our state. They will embrace the radical transgender agenda. They will persecute those they perceive to be enemies, especially Elon Musk. And in Washington, they will attack Trump every single day, constantly. Impeachment hearings, subpoenas, his family, cabinet members, business leaders, open persecution, and nonstop retaliation. Make no mistake. Nationally, the radicals are in charge. The communists and the Islamists who have taken over the Democrat Party have now taken over the United States Congress. They will be unleashed. Sadly, that means many Americans will be hurt. Texans will be hurt. Their assault on business will make Texas a much less attractive place to start or grow a small business. Texas will become more like California if they succeed in halting all new investment into AI. The economic results will be dramatic. Over $700 billion in new projects are scheduled to start in the next year. If the Democrats shut them all down, our country will very likely go into a recession. That will suit the Democrats just fine. They'll just blame it all on Donald Trump. In the next two years, we need to do two things. One, fight the madness. I will work with Democrats when they're willing to be reasonable. Last night, I called James Talarico. I congratulated him on his very impressive victory. It was a pleasant conversation, and I told him that I looked forward to working with him to try to benefit Texas. So, if there are things like flood relief for the Hill Country, or trying to get the space academy to Texas, he and I will work together. But if the newly elected radicals push policies that hurt Texas, raising taxes, destroying jobs, opening the border, releasing violent criminals, threatening our children, undermining our constitutional rights, I will fight with all of my strength to defend Texas and to defend the Constitution. And number two, we need to rebuild, getting behind policies that directly benefit the constituents we lost. There's a complicated story, no doubt, of what happened on Election Day, but as I see it, the key constituencies we lost were blue-collar voters, what had rightly become the core base of our party, Evangelical Christians, who didn't show up with the same numbers and fervor as prior elections, farmers and ranchers. Tragically, we alienated rural America. Young people, who excitedly had voted Republican in 2024, and who shifted hard blue this cycle. And of course, Hispanics. For Hispanics, there's a strong overlap with young people and blue-collar workers. In 2024, just two years ago, I was proud to carry Hispanics statewide in Texas by six points, and we swung the Rio Grande Valley red for the first time in a century. It can be done, but in this election, those Hispanic voters overwhelmingly went back Democrat. We have got to turn that around. And for young people, we need to be the party of the future. We need to champion policies that expand their future. Our two single biggest legislative accomplishments of the past two years, Trump Accounts and the school choice tax credit, which will unleash tens of billions of dollars in new scholarships for kids, are generationally powerful. I was proud to author both of those transformational policies, and yet too few candidates all across the country ran on that record. Too few voters were even aware of what we'd accomplished for their kids and their future. But we need to build. We need to expand to continue creating a new investor class for hundreds of millions of Americans, help everyone, every American, become an owner, to have real skin in the game, to create new generations of capitalists ready to reject socialism. People voted as they did because they were angry. Ironically, the Democrats that they elected are going to advance policies that will make affordability worse. The Democrats want gas prices higher. They want to ban gasoline engines altogether. Their extreme environmental mandates will drive up food prices and the prices of everything else. But hear me now: we will bring Texas back. I am filled with hope and optimism. Texas will be red again. We have not suddenly become a bunch of tofu-eating, gun-banning, tutu-wearing pinko commie liberals. That ain't us. Texas is still Texas. We will rebuild as a true blue-collar party, not by embracing socialism, but by being real free-market conservatives. The way we built the Texas economic miracle in the first place, and we will build and rebuild America as well. When the zealots overreach, and they will, we will stand ready to lead in the direction of freedom, of prosperity, of safety, and security, and common sense. We will return to a new dawn of freedom in America. It is dark right now, but it is always darkest before the dawn, and morning is coming. That is my fervent prayer, and that is my commitment to you. ## Dems Poised for Trifecta

This letter couldn't wait.

That's why Kirk Cameron personally asked me to write you on the
post-production budget shortfall for "Iggy and Mr. Kirk." He wanted to
make sure you heard about this urgent situation as soon as possible.

mission to help parents instill wholesome and Godly values in

[https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.

countering the Left's dangerous lies.

Lies like Drag Queens leading a Pride Parade SingAlong on Blue's

Same-sex weddings on Arthur...

And Sesame Street using YOUR tax dollars to normalize same-sex parents
and men in dresses.

And that's just what's on TV. Not to mention the thousands of 'Queer

The days of The Andy Griffith Show and Father Knows Best are gone. The
Left has purposely used TV to create a generation of zombie children
who are glued to their screens.

"Iggy and Mr. Kirk" is the antidote to that Leftist TV brainwashing.

It uses low-stimulation production and teaches children how to respond

Like when Mr. Kirk teaches Iggy:

Culture the Vulture says Iggy must become a human to fit in.
* to rely on the wisdom of parents -- one mom and one dad -- to
solve life's problems.
* to be BRAVE by speaking truth in the face of the Left's lies.

BRAVE FOR GOOD NEEDS TO RAISE $48,523 IN THE NEXT 4 WEEKS JUST FOR
"IGGY AND MR. KIRK."
[https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.

That doesn't even begin to account for our "Bible Revival" efforts and
the conservative Story Hours for the rest of the year.

Fellow Patriot, please help. Because this is so urgent, I wanted to
reach out to Americans who share our concern for the next generation.

On behalf of myself, Kirk, and our entire team, thank you for
considering supporting BRAVE FOR GOOD. Together, we will rebuild a
culture that honors God and His will for our lives.

Sincerely,

Dr. Trent Talbot

Founder, BRAVE for Good

while he's swamped with "See You at the Library Day," our "Bible
Revival" movement, and Season 3 of "Iggy and Mr. Kirk." I HOPE YOU CAN
HELP WITH YOUR TAX-DEDUCTIBLE GIFT OF $50, $100, OR EVEN $500. Thank
you for caring about America's families!

On Wednesday, Thomas Aquinas College published a study it commissioned from the Johns Hopkins Institute for Education Policy: a side-by-side of the verbal sections of three official SAT practice tests -- 1980, 1987, and 2026. The headline on the college's own summary is admirably blunt: shorter passages, less vocabulary, more time. Read it as an epitaph for a measurement.
In 1980, sixty of the eighty-five verbal questions -- 70.6 percent -- tested vocabulary straight on. Antonyms, analogies, sentence completions: formats where you either owned the word or you didn't, with no helpful sentence nearby to plead your case. 1987 held the line. On the 2026 test, ten questions -- 15 percent -- touch vocabulary at all, and every one hands you a sentence and asks you to fill a blank using the words around it. The definition of the word is in the room with you. It is the world's most elaborate method of never having to know anything cold.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f7119483-7020-44b7-8d6c-220ba9c13592?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The passages tell the same story. The old exams averaged 300 to 340 words and leaned on argumentative and persuasive writing -- the kind that assumed you had met the Enlightenment somewhere before. The 2026 test averages about 97 words per passage and supplies whatever background the question needs inside the text. Nothing is assumed, because nothing is left to assume. Even the clock relents: "more time" per question is the third leg of the retreat...

The SAT Stops Asking | | | Nov 5| | | ∙| | Preview ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | | On Wednesday, Thomas Aquinas College published a study it commissioned from the Johns Hopkins Institute for Education Policy: a side-by-side of the verbal sections of three official SAT practice tests -- 1980, 1987, and 2026. The headline on the college's own summary is admirably blunt: shorter passages, less vocabulary, more time. Read it as an epitaph for a measurement. In 1980, sixty of the eighty-five verbal questions -- 70.6 percent -- tested vocabulary straight on. Antonyms, analogies, sentence completions: formats where you either owned the word or you didn't, with no helpful sentence nearby to plead your case. 1987 held the line. On the 2026 test, ten questions -- 15 percent -- touch vocabulary at all, and every one hands you a sentence and asks you to fill a blank using the words around it. The definition of the word is in the room with you. It is the world's most elaborate method of never having to know anything cold. | | ---|---|--- The passages tell the same story. The old exams averaged 300 to 340 words and leaned on argumentative and persuasive writing -- the kind that assumed you had met the Enlightenment somewhere before. The 2026 test averages about 97 words per passage and supplies whatever background the question needs inside the text. Nothing is assumed, because nothing is left to assume. Even the clock relents: "more time" per question is the third leg of the retreat... Continue reading this post for free in the Substack app | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Heartland Journal 99 E. Every fraternity has a house. Some are known for the keg on the porch; some for the couch the fire marshal condemned in 1997. The house at 111 Taylor Street in San Francisco's Tenderloin is known for a different kind of brotherhood: at least 31 registered sex offenders, a guard at the door, and a weekly meditation group -- because even predators need help staying centered.
Welcome to rush week. It never ends. The California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation and the federal Bureau of Prisons keep offering bids, and the private GEO Group serves as house manager. The chapter sleeps 240, and the programming is genuinely inspiring: cultural diversity education, gender-responsive groups, and meditation. Nothing says rehabilitation quite like teaching a man to breathe deeply 400 feet from a daycare...

body:
A predator promised a mother a new life. Then one alarm changed everything.

| [View in Web Browser](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e6911774/VaHR0cHM6Ly93cm8ubnVjbGV1c2VtYWlsLmNvbS9hbXBsaWZ5L3YvUmRXc3VGQnBwSA/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDU/LbmNsOVJEU0dMYQ/qP2hpZHM9bmNCNzBJMDllc3g3WXJscw/gauyQ-g/s8l1c180932)
| | | [](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e6911774/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuc291bmRvZmZyZWVkb21mb3VuZGF0aW9uLm9yZy9zb2ZfbG9sYV8yMDI2X2FjcQ/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDU/LbmNsOVJEU0dMYQ/qP3NvdXJjZV9jb2RlPVdBUlIxNTc0NDcmdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fc291cmNlPWhhcmRhc2tfYWNxJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1zb2ZfbG9sYV8yMDI2/gauyQ-g/s4hc0f9fa64)
---
| |
---
| | God’s Children Are Not For Sale
---
|
---
| | | Friend,
---
My name is Eduardo Verástegui.

I am the producer of the film _Sound of Freedom_ and the founder of **Sound of Freedom Foundation.**

Years ago, I met the people who rescue children from trafficking. When I heard what is done to these children, I asked myself one question:

** _What if it were my child?_**

That question changed my life. And it is why I am writing to you today.

I want to tell you about a little girl. For her safety, we call her “Lola.”
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e6911774/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuc291bmRvZmZyZWVkb21mb3VuZGF0aW9uLm9yZy9zb2ZfbG9sYV8yMDI2X2FjcQ/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDU/LbmNsOVJEU0dMYQ/qP3NvdXJjZV9jb2RlPVdBUlIxNTc0NDcmdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fc291cmNlPWhhcmRhc2tfYWNxJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1zb2ZfbG9sYV8yMDI2/gauyQ-g/s4hc0f9fa64)
---
Lola’s mother was a hardworking single mom, doing everything she could for her little girl.

Then she met a man online.

He promised her the moon and the stars.

He traveled a long way to get them. He said his parents had a beautiful home in California and they would all be cared for.

**It was a lie.**

Soon, Lola and her mother were missing.

One of our house parents moved fast. Investigators believed the family had reached southern Mexico.

So she sounded the alarm.

**She worked with authorities to get an AMBER Alert out with Lola’s picture and pushed her case into the public eye.**
---
[ Sound the Alarm Now. Give Today ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e6911774/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuc291bmRvZmZyZWVkb21mb3VuZGF0aW9uLm9yZy9zb2ZfbG9sYV8yMDI2X2FjcQ/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDU/LbmNsOVJEU0dMYQ/qP3NvdXJjZV9jb2RlPVdBUlIxNTc0NDcmdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fc291cmNlPWhhcmRhc2tfYWNxJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1zb2ZfbG9sYV8yMDI2/gauyQ-g/s4hc0f9fa64)
---
And that very same day Lola was dropped off and left in front of child protective services.

Alone. Frightened. But alive.

Lola said her mother had died on the journey while she was crossing water. She could not swim.

We may never know what truly happened. But everything pointed to one terrible fear — that this man groomed her mother to get to her daughter. And that he planned to take Lola into the United States to be trafficked.

**But he did not get to keep her.**

**We stopped him.**

Today, Lola is safe. She was reunited with her grandparents and adopted by her loving aunt.
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e6911774/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuc291bmRvZmZyZWVkb21mb3VuZGF0aW9uLm9yZy9zb2ZfbG9sYV8yMDI2X2FjcQ/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDU/LbmNsOVJEU0dMYQ/qP3NvdXJjZV9jb2RlPVdBUlIxNTc0NDcmdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fc291cmNlPWhhcmRhc2tfYWNxJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1zb2ZfbG9sYV8yMDI2/gauyQ-g/s4hc0f9fa64)
---
Friend, this is not a movie.

About two million children are exploited in the sex trade around the world, according to the U.S. State Department.

**Two million. Each one made in the image of God.**

Our nation was built on the belief that every life has worth because God gave it.

**That truth does not let us look away.**

Jesus said, “ _Let the little children come to me, and do not hinder them, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these._ ” (Matthew 19:14 NIV)

That is why **Sound of Freedom Foundation** exists — **to stop the sale of God’s children.**

And Lola’s story shows the most important truth of all: **children are found when people pay attention.**

Here is how you can join the fight today:

1\. **Stay alert.** Traffickers often start online with kindness and big promises.

2\. **If you see something, say something**. Read every AMBER Alert. Share it. If something feels wrong, call 911 or report a trafficking tip through **Sound of Freedom Foundation's** partner, Rescue America, at 1-833-599-3733.

3.**Make your first gift**. Help **Sound of Freedom Foundation** and our partners keep sounding the alarm.
---
[ Sound the Alarm Now. Give Today ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e6911774/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuc291bmRvZmZyZWVkb21mb3VuZGF0aW9uLm9yZy9zb2ZfbG9sYV8yMDI2X2FjcQ/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDU/LbmNsOVJEU0dMYQ/qP3NvdXJjZV9jb2RlPVdBUlIxNTc0NDcmdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fc291cmNlPWhhcmRhc2tfYWNxJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1zb2ZfbG9sYV8yMDI2/gauyQ-g/s4hc0f9fa64)
---
Your gift helps equip investigators to find children fast, sound the alarm through film and media, support house parents who welcome rescued children home, and teach everyone the warning signs.

[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e6911774/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuc291bmRvZmZyZWVkb21mb3VuZGF0aW9uLm9yZy9zb2ZfbG9sYV8yMDI2X2FjcQ/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDU/LbmNsOVJEU0dMYQ/qP3NvdXJjZV9jb2RlPVdBUlIxNTc0NDcmdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fc291cmNlPWhhcmRhc2tfYWNxJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1zb2ZfbG9sYV8yMDI2/gauyQ-g/s4hc0f9fa64)[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e6911774/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuc291bmRvZmZyZWVkb21mb3VuZGF0aW9uLm9yZy9zb2ZfbG9sYV8yMDI2X2FjcQ/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDU/LbmNsOVJEU0dMYQ/qP3NvdXJjZV9jb2RlPVdBUlIxNTc0NDcmdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fc291cmNlPWhhcmRhc2tfYWNxJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1zb2ZfbG9sYV8yMDI2/gauyQ-g/s4hc0f9fa64)**[Will you give $25, $50, $75, $100, or whatever you can right now to help sound the alarm for the next child like Lola?](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e6911774/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuc291bmRvZmZyZWVkb21mb3VuZGF0aW9uLm9yZy9zb2ZfbG9sYV8yMDI2X2FjcQ/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDU/LbmNsOVJEU0dMYQ/qP3NvdXJjZV9jb2RlPVdBUlIxNTc0NDcmdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fc291cmNlPWhhcmRhc2tfYWNxJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1zb2ZfbG9sYV8yMDI2/gauyQ-g/s4hc0f9fa64)**

When good people keep quiet, they become part of the problem.

But when good people speak up, **God’s children come home.**

Tonight, a child is waiting to be found. You can be the one who steps in right now.

I want to tell you about a little girl. For her safety, we call her “Lola.” Lola’s mother was a hardworking single mom, doing everything she could for her little girl. Then she met a man online. He promised her the moon and the stars. He traveled a long way to get them. He said his parents had a beautiful home in California and they would all be cared for. It was a lie. Soon, Lola and her mother were missing. One of our house parents moved fast. Investigators believed the family had reached southern Mexico. So she sounded the alarm. She worked with authorities to get an AMBER Alert out with Lola’s picture and pushed her case into the public eye. And that very same day Lola was dropped off and left in front of child protective services. Alone. Frightened. But alive. Lola said her mother had died on the journey while she was crossing water. She could not swim. We may never know what truly happened. But everything pointed to one terrible fear — that this man groomed her mother to get to her daughter. And that he planned to take Lola into the United States to be trafficked. But he did not get to keep her. We stopped him. Today, Lola is safe. She was reunited with her grandparents and adopted by her loving aunt. Friend, this is not a movie. About two million children are exploited in the sex trade around the world, according to the U.S. State Department. Two million. Each one made in the image of God. Our nation was built on the belief that every life has worth because God gave it. That truth does not let us look away. Jesus said, “ Let the little children come to me, and do not hinder them, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these. ” (Matthew 19:14 NIV) That is why Sound of Freedom Foundation exists — to stop the sale of God’s children. And Lola’s story shows the most important truth of all: children are found when people pay attention. Here is how you can join the fight today: 1\. Stay alert. Traffickers often start online with kindness and big promises. 2\. If you see something, say something. Read every AMBER Alert. Share it. If something feels wrong, call 911 or report a trafficking tip through Sound of Freedom Foundation's partner, Rescue America, at 1-833-599-3733. 3.Make your first gift. Help Sound of Freedom Foundation and our partners keep sounding the alarm. Your gift helps equip investigators to find children fast, sound the alarm through film and media, support house parents who welcome rescued children home, and teach everyone the warning signs. When good people keep quiet, they become part of the problem. But when good people speak up, God’s children come home. Tonight, a child is waiting to be found. You can be the one who steps in right now. God’s children are not for sale. With gratitude and prayer, Eduardo Verástegui Sound of Freedom, Producer For Sound of Freedom Foundation P.S. One alarm. One picture. One day. That is all it took for Lola to be set free. Please make your first gift today and help us sound the alarm for the next child. | Sound of Freedom Foundation is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization. All donations are tax deductible as permissible by law and used where needed most. PO Box 131727, Houston, TX 77219

Team, Elections around the country, from a U.S. Senate race in Mississippi down to local offices, could still come down to a handful of votes. In some cases, these are ballots that have been provisionally cast; in others, they are mail-in ballots with a small error that need to be "cured;" and in a lot of states, there are still valid, eligible ballots arriving in the so-called "grace period." That's where a ballot has been mailed and postmarked _before_ Election Day but is delivered in the next few business days _after_ Election Day. These ballots need to be counted. Voters who can fix and "cure" their ballots deserve the chance to do so. That's a key part of our fundamental right to vote. **[We hate to ask after all you've done so far, but will you pitch in with $35 or whatever you can to help us make every vote count in our elections?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142947688/658580008/-1725532854?refcode=110526_2&amount=35&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAwNy8xLzg5MjE1IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjc5ODBiMmI4LTI5ZDktZjExMS1iZjViLTAwMGQzYTU0NDQyZSIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=fqhhCvrROkIzmNirj2iXnZlgwTow4e68BiN3SCP0mQk=)**

Opponents of voting rights have attacked these mail-in ballot grace periods in the past and will be doing everything they can to get ballots tossed in this election or the next if we don't fight them. In a 5-4 decision back in June, the Supreme Court rejected arguments that federal laws setting Election Day preempted states from accepting ballots after that federally set date. This issue and so many others relating to mail-in voting rest on a knife's edge, where a differently argued case might have lost. We can't afford to lose vital protections for mail-in voting, not after all the progress this week. States count thousands of ballots after Election Day, from grace period ballots to votes provisionally cast to cured ballots. These votes deserve the same equitable treatment as the votes cast in-person during early voting or on Election Day. **November 5, 2026**
One of the sweetest chores in this time of holiday cheer has nothing to do with relaxing.
Preparing to make sugar syrup is work I have usually done by myself. There is something deeply personal about it, a creative connection between my hands and the harvest, just me and Nature.
"How can I help you, Ivette?"
I cut down the cane. She peeled the leaves. We hauled the stalks to the working station. I cut each one just so. She rinsed the pieces and placed them into the pots where they would turn, then filled the pots with water. Together, we lifted each one onto the fire.
We peered into the pots periodically, as one is wont to do after all that work . . .
Tiffany is my daughter-in-law. We were alongside one another that one season.
I watch the color change, the stalks soften, and breathe in the sweet aroma as it wafts throughout the house. After a measure of time, there it is: that deep golden, amber thickness, with a beauty and sweetness all its own.
I remember Tiffany, but on this day I remember her not with a heaviness of heart for the life she did not get to live, nor with sorrow for what I could not change, but with joy for the work we shared, through which I came to know her for who she was and who she wanted to be.
**Pause.
Breathe.
Look Deeper.**
**Refuel.**
**Welcome to Sweet Ground.**

On June 10, 2026, schoolteachers in one of the poorest corners of Louisiana opened the richest envelopes of their careers.
The checks came from the Richland Parish School Board's annual "13th check" -- a year-end bonus paid out of a local _sales tax_ that, for as long as anyone could remember, generated modest little stipends. The year before, vested teachers got about $10,000. That was already remarkable; most parishes pay nothing of the kind. This year, vested, certified teachers received $50,900. Support staff received more than $17,000. In some cases the bonus doubled a teacher's _annual salary_.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4314856c-f3d6-438d-8e1a-9a4a8e162267?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Richland Parish is a farming community of roughly 19,800 people in Louisiana's northeastern corner, with about 3,000 students and 164 classroom teachers. The median household income is about $53,500. Read those numbers together and you understand what actually happened: _a single bonus check equal to an entire year 's household income_, delivered not by a federal program, not by a grant application, not by an equity initiative -- but by a construction site.
**The Engine**
The engine is Meta's Hyperion data center near Holly Ridge, outside the parish seat of Rayville. Announced in December 2024 as a $10 billion, 2-gigawatt campus, it has since been expanded to 5 gigawatts, with cost estimates now running from $27 billion to $50 billion. It is projected to cover about six square miles and draw seven times as much electricity as the city of New Orleans. It is the _largest private investment in the history of Louisiana_.
The tax consequences were immediate. For the first nine months of the fiscal year, the parish collected $42.9 million in sales and use tax -- more than double the prior year, according to the Northwest Louisiana Finance Authority. Sandie Lollie, president of the Northeast Federation of Teachers and School Employees, put the school-dedicated share more vividly: "The taxes grew almost 2,000%." Meta also cut the parish a separate $22.4 million tax payment in May. More than $1.6 billion in contracts have gone to Louisiana businesses since construction began.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/40066bfb-28e5-492b-af4b-1077f2d85cf2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Nobody Had to Redesign Anything**
Here is the detail that should make this story the conservative parable of the decade: _the mechanism predates the data center by decades_.
Richland Parish voters approved a dedicated school sales tax long before anyone in Rayville had heard of artificial intelligence. The "13th check" was already law, already administered, already funded. When Meta's capital crashed into that existing structure, the checks simply got bigger. No new agency. No federal compliance officer. No application, no means test, no pilot program with a five-year evaluation.
Washington's answer to underpaid rural teachers is always the same: a new program, a new office, a new acronym, and a takeaway for administration. Northeast Louisiana's answer was to make the parish a place where someone wanted to build something so enormous that the existing tax base doubled -- and the teachers got their cut, exactly as the voters who set up the tax always intended.
This is what it looks like when private capital does the work that redistribution only promises. The average federal teacher-quality program spends millions on administration to move thousands. Hyperion moved the actual money into actual local bank accounts in one fiscal year.
**" But Can It Last?"**
The objections arrived on schedule, so let's take them in order.
**First** : it's a sugar high. The New York Times ran the story under the headline "The A.I. Boom Boosted Teacher Pay in a Rural County. Can It Last?" -- and the point is fair. Data centers employ relatively few permanent workers once the cranes leave. Sales tax will normalize when construction ends.
But notice what the critics concede in making this argument. Superintendent Sheldon Jones anticipates "elevated bonuses for the duration of the Hyperion construction project" -- which is to say, for years, in a parish that had no comparable revenue source at all. Construction is a multi-year event, the windfall compounds, and Jones notes the multiplier effect: other industries are already looking at Richland Parish because the growth is visible. Neighboring parishes, the trade press reports, are now actively recruiting data centers of their own. The alternative on the table was not permanent prosperity. It was a parish that had been emptying out for a generation, collecting zero.
**Second** : corporate welfare. A Sherwood News analysis, picked up by Fortune, tallies roughly $3.3 billion in tax incentives Meta negotiated -- sales-and-use exemptions on its own equipment under Act 730, property tax abatements, a payments-in-lieu arrangement. The Times followed with an investigation titled "How Meta Got Everything It Wanted in a Secret Louisiana Data Center Deal."
Two responses. The first is arithmetic: an incentive is foregone revenue on a project that would not otherwise exist. The counterfactual was never Meta paying full freight in Richland Parish. It was Meta building in another state, and Richland Parish continuing its long decline with its pristine, un-discounted tax base -- still generating almost nothing. A 90%-off coupon on a $30 billion investment is a better deal than 100% of nothing.
The second response is to notice the irony. The same progressive commentators who shrug at billions in federal subsidies for politically favored industries -- EV credits, green-energy grants, Chips Act slush -- have discovered the phrase "corporate welfare" for a project that is actually building something, in a place the federal government forgot, and that just handed rural schoolteachers five-figure checks. Their objection is not that the money was wasted. It is that the money worked.
**Third** : the strain AKA real cost. Roads, water, the grid -- a project drawing seven times New Orleans' power is a genuine infrastructure event. Concede it plainly. It is also what the $22.4 million payment, and the payments that follow it, are for. Those are the growing pains of growth, which is a categorically different problem from the shrinking pains of decline Richland Parish had grown expert at managing.
**" Like Nobody's Ever Seen"**
President Trump says America is building data centers like nobody has ever seen before. For once, the boast undersells the record. In one rural Louisiana parish, an AI buildout doubled the local tax base in a single year and cut schoolteachers checks equal to a year's household income -- through a tax mechanism the voters themselves created, administered by a school board, with no one in Washington involved at any step of the transaction.
Major teachers' unions--primarily the National Education Association (NEA) and the **[American Federation of Teachers](https://substack.com/redirect/d2264926-009d-4004-93af-f2c78945330a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** (AFT)--have consistently directed **at least 94 percent** (with some reports and cycle estimates showing **98 to 99 percent**) of their direct candidate and political party contributions to Democrats. Does Republican Speaker of the House from Louisiana not now this?
That is the real contrast in American politics right now, and it is not between "pro-education" and "anti-education." It is between two theories of how teachers get paid more. One theory runs money through the federal government and calls whatever dribbles out a victory. The other theory builds a $30 billion machine in a cotton field and lets a parish sales tax do the rest.
Richland Parish chose the second theory. Its teachers got $50,900. Nobody had to fill out a federal form -- except Meta, for the bonuses' withholding, and it was glad to.

name: Dr. Robert Jeffress
subject: Your invitation to a year of spiritual growth

name: Chuck Rocha
subject: The Latino Vote in 2026: What We Built and What Comes Next
body:
The Latino vote shifted in 2026. Read Chuck Rocha's New York Times op-ed on what drove the gains and what comes next. | | | |
---
| | |
#### **The Latino Vote in 2026:
What We Built and What Comes Next**
---
|
---
| Friends,

The 2026 midterms marked a historic moment for Latino political engagement in America, and we're proud of the role Solidarity Strategies played in helping campaigns reach communities across the country through a multi-media, culturally competent winning strategy.

For decades, Latino voters have been overlooked in modern political communications, with Spanish-language outreach too often treated as an afterthought. This cycle, Democratic Leadership challenged that approach through unprecedented investments in Latino outreach, bilingual messaging, creative storytelling, and direct voter contact.

---
|
---
**_Campaigns Solidarity Strategies supported throughout the 2026 election cycle_**
| We worked on a combination of 32 competitive Senate, House, and Gubernatorial races this year in states and districts with significant Latino electorates to bring their messages to life by connecting the economic pain families were experiencing, raising questions about failed Republican leadership and corruption, and presenting the Democratic platform as an alternative offering solutions–all in English and Spanish.

**In a new New York Times op-ed, our founder and president Chuck Rocha reflects on the Latino vote in 2026, the lessons Democrats should take from this election, and why continued investment will be essential in the cycles ahead.**

[**Read Chuck Rocha's New York Times op-ed here**](https://us.list-manage.com/12tylKxj6Yy?e=b8f90417f9&c2id=150df94da93954b2128cfda2414939d1)

We should not mistake one election's progress for a permanent political realignment. Election Day may be behind us, but the work of earning and maintaining voters' trust is far from over.

¡Pa'lante!

**The Solidarity Strategies Team**

subject: A triumph for our district

body:
Thank you for everything

| Peter, there really are moments when words fail.

Yesterday was Election Day, and I'm still not sure I know how to tell you what this win means to me. I've tried to put my gratitude into words a dozen different ways, and every time, “thank you” doesn't seem like nearly enough.

Right now, I'm thinking about the people who gave up their evenings and weekends to knock on doors, who spent hours making phone calls, who donated money they had worked hard to earn, and who kept believing in this campaign even when we faced impossible odds. I wish I could thank each of you in person.

**It's hard to explain what this victory means without going back to the little girl I used to be.** Growing up, I never imagined I would run for office, let alone have the opportunity to serve in Congress. Politics felt a world away from our trailer door. When my Dad got sick, my family lost everything. We were figuring out what came next day by day, and I certainly wasn't imagining a future like this.

What I had, though, was a family who loved me, taught me to work hard, and showed me what it meant to keep going when life didn't go according to plan. My parents did everything they could to help me reach my potential, and my public school teachers helped me forge a path where I could get ahead and use my voice to help others do the same.

That's why I kept running for Congress. Despite the losses, every time I talked with a parent worried about their family's future, a farmer trying to keep their operation going, or a small-business owner struggling to stay afloat, I was reminded why I ran in the first place. **And this time, we did it.**

We built an extraordinary team and ran a campaign focused on the people of Iowa. We knocked on tens of thousands of doors, raised the resources to compete against a powerful political machine, and kept showing up, day after day. I think about the conversations on front porches, the people who opened their homes and told me about their lives, the volunteers who gave up their weekends, and the supporters who invested time and money to give this campaign a fighting chance.

I can't promise every challenge will have an easy answer, but I can promise I will bring everything I have to this responsibility. I'll keep you informed about what I'm doing, and I'll make sure the issues you care about are always front and center. I have so many plans for what we'll achieve for our district together, and so many things I'm dying to work on that I can barely sit still. I can't wait to officially be your representative, and I hope to make you proud.

Thank you for everything,

Christina P.S. I think about the conversations on front porches, the people who opened their homes and told me about their lives, the volunteers who gave up their weekends, and the supporters who invested time and money to give this campaign a fighting chance. I can't promise every challenge will have an easy answer, but I can promise I will bring everything I have to this responsibility. I'll keep you informed about what I'm doing, and I'll make sure the issues you care about are always front and center. I have so many plans for what we'll achieve for our district together, and so many things I'm dying to work on that I can barely sit still. I can't wait to officially be your representative, and I hope to make you proud. Thank you for everything, Christina P.S. | | | | | | Team Mackenzie,All I can say is thank you. Thank you for being part of something bigger than all of us and for showing your support in so many different ways.This campaign had it all. We had people willing to knock on doors, make phone calls, write postcards, work at the polls, and contribute financially. I am deeply humbled by the support our team has received and incredibly grateful for every person who gave their time, energy, and money.Two years ago, we set out to make a difference in the Lehigh Valley, and I am proud to say that we did. With your help, you sent me to Congress, where we resolved thousands of constituent cases, secured funding for community projects and first responders, and cast critical votes that helped the people of the Lehigh Valley and our beloved country.Obviously, the results did not go the way we had hoped. We saw crushing losses across the country. But I ask you not to give up. We won a race in 2024 that we were not supposed to win because people refused to give up and gave it their all. We gave it our all this year, but we came up short. That does not mean we will always come up short. It means we buckle down, learn from this experience, and work even harder.It has truly been an honor to serve as your congressman, and I will not stop working to deliver for the community I love.Thank you, and God bless you.Congressman Ryan Mackenzie

name: API PA
subject: We made history. Thank you.
body:
This moment is exactly why API PA exists.
| |
---
| Dear Peter, Yesterday I was in Dauphin County, surrounded by API PA’s team and our partners CASA in Action and One Pennsylvania with one message: Time’s up. Time’s up on the wealthy getting wealthier while people struggle to keep a roof over their heads. Time’s up on billions of dollars for wars and ICE prisons and no money for schools and healthcare. Time’s up on tax breaks for gambling, data centers, and crypto scams while manufacturing, agriculture, and public service jobs disappear. Across Pennsylvania and across the Commonwealth, our elections weren’t just about the candidates. They were about us. How we pay the rent. How we take care of our children. How we work, how we love, and how we live as a community. API PA voters delivered. Our field teams knocked 100,000 doors, made over 3 million calls, and had over 50,000 conversations with AAPI voters. In Congressional District 10, API PA worked with community partners to organize Nepali-Bhutanese refugees who were targets of ICE deportations and Scott Perry’s anti-immigrant vitriol. Nothing made me prouder than witnessing two amazing refugee women leaders head up API PA’s civic engagement, organizing, and field efforts that threw out Scott Perry and ushered in new leadership.
* In Pennsylvania’s 1st Congressional District, we helped elect Bob Harvie and flip a critical congressional seat, knocking on nearly 26,000 doors in Bensalem alone.
* In Pennsylvania Senate District 6, we were proud to support Eileen Abillar and help flip one of four state senate seats that delivered a Democratic trifecta in Harrisburg for the first time in decades.
* Our year-round phone banking team also helped deliver AAPI voters to power victories in North Carolina, Texas, and Arizona.

On Election Day, we showed what can happen when we organize, engage, and mobilize for each other. We don't just win elections — we fundamentally shift the balance of power. API PA exists to turn grassroots energy into lasting political power for Asian American and diverse immigrant communities across this Commonwealth so that our voices can never be ignored. **I am writing to you today to say thank you. Thank you to every single volunteer, member, donor, and supporter who made this possible. You built a movement. You made history.** **[If this work matters to you, keep supporting API PA by donating here or joining us as a member!](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/4LUf8Ftk1Sr9yLuKqj1tQRKZRz7CjltH/click?signature=cdec22d07f80cc7ea4d6f3264b43193ba4e366ee&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.apipennsylvania.org%2Fmembership)** Our work is just beginning. It’s one thing to win an election. It’s another thing to prove that an election will actually make a difference in our people’s lives. Alongside a growing and diverse coalition, API PA is gearing up to make sure our legislature and our elected officials fight for the people who put them there. Stay tuned. Stay active. Stay hopeful. In solidarity, Helen Gym Interim Executive Director, API PA
---

---

The election, or, if you're a Republican, the total and complete beating, is now two days behind us. In Mississippi, the GOP is still counting absentee ballots and hoping for a "win" in the Senate race between Cindy Hyde-Smith and Scott Colom. A final result could be days away. But even if the GOP pulls it out by a handful of votes we need to ask: what does this beatdown tell us?
There's a lot to learn. CNN and its socialist friends will tell you it means Americans have embraced their agenda and are ready to follow Venezuela, China, Cuba, and a long list of other failed countries down their preferred socialist path. Some will tell you it's your fault because you didn't vote, you anti-American fool. At least, that's what they think of you. Others will say it's because we didn't support Israel vigorously enough. Never mind that we've sent billions upon billions of dollars already. And if you object, they'll call you an anti-Semite. How dare you not want to put your kids in debt for Netanyahu and his band of warmongers? For the record, I don't believe for one second that God expects you or me to risk our nation's future to support a secular government run by fallible men. Even if you believe God's promise to the nation of Israel has not yet been fulfilled, nothing in God's word says I must let a man lead my nation into economic destruction.
So what happened? Start with the Republican Party itself. Can you tell me what exactly the GOP stands for today? In Mississippi, most of our local officials put an R behind their names. But have you ever asked one of them to explain the Republican Party platform? Most of them couldn't tell you there is a platform, and the ones who know about it don't care. That makes our local "Republican" officials completely useless at governing by the standards of the party, standards that most of the citizens in their towns actually believe in.
Next, consider your state representative and senator. They also call themselves Republicans, but do they actually care about conservative policy? Mine certainly don't. They treat their office as an excuse to spend a few months a year away from their families having fun in the big city of Jackson. When they're "in session," you and conservative policy are the last things on their minds.
Mississippi has a reputation as a conservative state. Is it, really? Supposedly we have great gun laws. Here's a test. Last year, President Trump and Congress zeroed out the $200 federal tax on firearm suppressors, and this fall the ATF announced it would stop enforcing the federal registration requirement. Great news for gun owners, right? Not so fast. Mississippi law says you can only own a suppressor if you're "authorized under federal law." In other words, your gun rights in "conservative" Mississippi depend on whoever happens to be running the ATF in Washington. Our own Attorney General has warned that a future administration could reverse the change and has asked the Legislature to cut the federal reference out of our law. Bills to fix it have been filed before, and our "conservative" Legislature never got it done. That isn't conservative leadership. It's a bunch of politicians who like the conservative label but always take the easy way out. Following is not leading.
And if you want to bring up the abortion law that went to the Supreme Court and overturned Roe v. Wade, let me tell you what I saw with my own eyes. I watched Republicans in the House Republican Caucus beg the Speaker to kill that bill because they didn't want to deal with the fallout of voting on another pro-life measure. Our Legislature is full of, and run by, some of the weakest, most mind-numbingly spineless people you'll ever meet. They care only about getting back to Jackson every year so they can pretend to be important.
Then there's our "representation" in Washington. Unless you're deeply involved in the Republican Party, I don't know a single citizen who thinks Roger Wicker or Cindy Hyde-Smith are great examples of conservatives fighting for the people of Mississippi. Local and state politicians love them because they bring home cash, which is really just your money cycled through the federal government, so those politicians can grow government while still pretending to be conservative. Beyond that, nobody believes our senators or our field of wet-noodle congressmen fight for anything other than themselves and big government.
Then there's President Trump. Most of us enthusiastically voted for him and had high hopes that he would be the leader this nation needs. And honestly, the first year of his hard-fought second term was fantastic. He hit D.C. like a man with a plan. He promised to fix the border, fix the economy, end the war between Russia and Ukraine, and stop the cycle of war after war after war.
Ukraine proved harder than he expected, and most of us didn't blame him for that. We still trusted that, with his help, the war would end sooner rather than later, and that at the very least we would stop spending ourselves into bankruptcy supporting it. He fixed the border in short order. That's one issue, maybe the only one, we can all call a huge success. He brought Elon Musk to D.C. to start wringing out waste and fraud. But Trump found out what the rest of us already knew: nobody else in Washington, especially the Republicans in the House and Senate, cared one bit about eliminating waste, fraud, and abuse. In fact, most of us are convinced they support all of it. Not a single one of our "conservative" representatives in D.C. lifted a finger to help Trump or Musk save this country from the economic disaster ahead.
And let's not forget Trump made two more promises: no war with Iran, and the release of the Epstein files, so that the pedophile and human-trafficking ring of government officials and big-business leaders would finally be exposed and prosecuted. What do we have instead? An endless war with Iran, and a Justice Department, Congress, and executive branch that have decided to protect the pedophiles at the expense of their victims and the American people. Thomas Massie led the fight to release the Epstein files while nearly every Republican in Congress stood on the sidelines. For his trouble, Trump and the GOP turned on him.
So, you want to know why Republicans lost Tuesday? It's simple. No one believes they make any difference at all. They don't believe in anything. They aren't conservative. They have zero interest in anything but serving themselves, growing government, and continuing the waste, fraud, and abuse.
Where do we go from here? As a nation, the honest answer is down. We are headed toward Cuba and Venezuela. If you're waiting on the GOP to slow that down, you'll still be waiting when you're standing in the bread line.
The only answer is for you to change the direction. Start with your mayor, your county supervisor, your state representative and senator, your governor and lieutenant governor, because D.C. is all but lost. Outside of Rand Paul, Thomas Massie, and a handful of fighters in the House Freedom Caucus, all that's left there are useless Republicans and socialist Democrats, and a few good men can't hold back the tide by themselves. So hunker down, fix your community and your state, and ride out the storm. A storm is coming. Trump and the GOP opened the floodgates, and a wave of socialist Democrats is about to pour through.
Hold on. This ain't going to be fun.

**Thursday, November 5, 2026 -**_****_
_**Iran:** Vice President JD Vance blames Republican election losses on Iran war; Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf accuses U.S. of putting Israel first. CBS: Trump asks advisers if he should remove War Secretary Pete Hegseth. NYT: SCOTUS justice Samuel Alito privately says he won't retire immediately, despite Democrats' Senate win. House Speaker Mike Johnson will not seek leadership role. Billionaire Leon Black sues Rep. Robert Garcia for defamation over remarks about Epstein ties._
_**International:** World Health Organization approves Ebola vaccine trials for dangerous Bundibugyo strain. Sudanese Army strike in North Kordofan kills two women, destroys water station. Ethiopia, Sudan close each other's consulates. Workers strike and march across France. Russian and Ukraine exchange attacks; Russia kills four civilians in Donetsk. Syria secures $400+ million Saudi loan in new defense agreement. Stabbing attack outside Sri Lanka embassy in Jordan kills security officer. Colombia expected to pass law toughening terms of surrender for armed group, breaking with "total peace" policy. UN elects five judges to International Court of Justice. Bomb threats disrupt European air travel._

* * *
# Iran
* **Vance blames Republican election losses on Iran war; Iran 's Ghalibaf accuses U.S. of putting Israel first: **The Iran war was the main reason Republicans lost the 2026 midterm elections, U.S. Vice President JD Vance [wrote](https://substack.com/redirect/2f3a7211-6ba0-46a4-8868-21f05acab7f0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Thursday, arguing that voters who backed President Donald Trump in 2024 switched to supporting Democrats despite strong Republican turnout.
* Citing private polling that he said accurately anticipated the results, Vance identified four leading reasons former Trump voters abandoned Republicans: "End the war," "Focus on cost of living/inflation," "Put America First," and "Change our relationship to Israel."
* He said the findings vindicated calls for a diplomatic resolution to the conflict, and he warned against attributing the losses to the Trump administration's far-right immigration policies. "The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night," Vance wrote. "If you'd like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so."
* Responding to Vance, Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf [accused](https://substack.com/redirect/7ca8e4f3-c75b-474e-8bd0-0a9b1f664717?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the Trump administration of preparing another phase of the conflict while prioritizing Israel over American interests. "Boss is prepping the next war phase while America teeters on an Israel-First cliff," Ghalibaf wrote, adding: "Why not say this to your boss?"
* **Iran 's Khamenei says U.S. midterm results will not change Washington's hostility toward Tehran: **Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei said on Wednesday that anyone expecting a change in U.S. policy following Republican losses in the midterm elections is "seriously mistaken."
* "Those who still harbor even the slightest hope that the behavior of the hegemonic system might change through partisan or factional shifts . . . are seriously mistaken," Khamenei said in a written statement published on his website.
* **Iran says two tankers, tugboat catch fire in Strait of Hormuz; UK reports tanker attacked near Qatar:** Two oil tankers [caught fire](https://substack.com/redirect/bbecabf7-a17d-4ce1-832f-a6e8a608b359?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in separate incidents in the Strait of Hormuz after attempting to use "unauthorized" shipping routes, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy said on Thursday. A tugboat attempting to extinguish the fire also caught fire.
* A tanker was struck by two unidentified projectiles approximately 50 nautical miles north of Madinat Al-Shamal, Qatar, the UK Maritime Trade Operations reported on Thursday. The condition of the crew and the extent of damage remain unconfirmed.
* **South Korea plans to expand naval mission near Strait of Hormuz:** South Korea [plans](https://substack.com/redirect/600f4625-49a7-4a56-9741-c2f57045bbf7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to expand its anti-piracy naval mission in the Gulf of Aden toward waters south of Oman, near the Strait of Hormuz, and deploy additional military assets, Yonhap reported on Thursday.
* It would be Seoul's first military contribution to maritime security efforts in the region since the U.S.-Iran war began in February. In September, South Korea declined U.S. requests for direct military support against Tehran.
* South Korean defense officials stressed that the mission would not involve combat forces and would remain independent of allied military operations. They said that aircraft will be prohibited from monitoring Iranian territory or entering the Strait of Hormuz.
* **U.S. sanctions Indian, Turkish firms over alleged ties to Iranian oil, aviation:** On Wednesday, the U.S. Treasury Department [imposed](https://substack.com/redirect/41642233-fb49-428c-9830-849f4dee9243?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) sanctions on individuals and companies in India and Turkey over their alleged support for Iran's oil and aviation sectors, as part of the Trump administration's Operation Economic Outcast campaign to restrict Iranian oil revenues during the war.
* The Treasury Department accused Indian entities of falsifying vessel registrations for ships transporting Iranian oil. It also sanctioned Turkey-based Fugo Ground Services Inc. for supporting Iran's aviation sector.
* The Treasury Department said last week that its sanctions campaign had contributed to the collapse of Iran's currency and increased inflation almost 90%.
* **UAE airline profits plunge 66% amid Iran war:** The Dubai-based Emirates Group airline sustained a 66% decline in its after-tax profits, it [said](https://substack.com/redirect/a54e0f40-352d-4210-bd4c-dc7d59983294?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Thursday. Year-on-year, the airline's profit fell to $1 billion in the first half of its 2026-27 financial year, as the Iran war disrupted air travel and pushed up fuel costs. The Emirates airline carried 21.8 million passengers between April and September, down 22% from a year earlier. The company said that it remained profitable despite the disruptions, with cash reserves declining to $14.7 billion by the end of September.

# Palestine
* **Israeli attacks kill three Palestinians, including child, in Gaza:** Israeli forces [shot and killed](https://substack.com/redirect/801b1ea4-3d89-4b56-8bc3-671a68fa616a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a woman in Al-Mawasi, west of Khan Younis in southern Gaza, and a child in the Bureij refugee camp in central Gaza on Thursday, WAFA reported. Another Palestinian was killed in an Israeli airstrike west of Al-Zawayda in central Gaza.
* **Israeli settlers seize homes near Jericho, expelling Palestinians; settlers say they are "dismantling the Oslo Accords": **Around 30 Israeli settlers, some of whom were armed, [took over](https://substack.com/redirect/020fee11-a482-45eb-98f4-799fdaa63921?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) eight homes in Ein Al-Duyuk Al-Tahta on the outskirts of Jericho in the occupied West Bank on Wednesday. Activists warned that settlers could be reproducing the situation in Hebron, where armed Israeli settlers live in enclaves inside the Palestinian city, contributing to displacement and severe restrictions on Palestinian freedom of mobility. The operation near Jericho was organized by the Nachala settlement movement, which claims to have secretly purchased the properties.
* Sixty-five Palestinian residents fled after settlers attacked them with stones, an activist [told](https://substack.com/redirect/a5edc179-7c5a-46ea-866f-f26da7301d00?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the Times of Israel. Residents said that Israeli forces subsequently blocked access to the area, leaving homeowners afraid to return.
* The new outpost is reportedly located in Area C, under full Israeli control under the Oslo Accords, just meters from parts of Jericho classified as Area A, where the Palestinian Authority is supposed to exercise civilian and security control.
* Yisrael Gantz, head of the West Bank settler council, framed the move as an effort to dismantle the Oslo Accords, declaring: "Today we begin reversing the trend, dismantling the Oslo Accords through actions, house by house, family by family."
* Palestinian National Council Speaker Rawhi Fattouh condemned the takeover as "organized terrorism" carried out under Israeli government protection, charging Israel of encouraging settlement expansion and forced displacement.
* **Israel demolishes five buildings, displacing 105 Palestinians, and shuts down club in occupied East Jerusalem:** Israeli forces [demolished](https://substack.com/redirect/817b136c-86d7-4afb-92ab-0dac89dab213?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) five residential buildings containing 12 apartments in the town of Biddu, northwest of occupied East Jerusalem, on Thursday, displacing 105 Palestinians without prior warning, citing construction without permits. # U.S. News
* **Democrats extend power in House, state races in latest midterm election results:** Additional races were called on Wednesday, extending Democrats' commanding lead in the House of Representatives and in state-level posts. Senate elections in Mississippi and Alaska remain uncalled as of Thursday morning, while an unexpectedly tight Senate race in Louisiana was called in favor of the Republican, **Julia Letlow.**
* **Sam Forstag,** a labor union leader and smokejumper endorsed by Rep. **Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez** , won his election to represent Montana's first congressional district, a seat previously held by Trump's former Interior Secretary, **Ryan Zinke**. He is also the youngest congressional representative from the state since the 1930s.

* Republican incumbent Rep. **Max Miller** , who was accused of physical and verbal abuse by his ex-wife, conceded defeat to Democrat **Brian Poindexter** in Ohio's seventh congressional district, which covers much of the Cleveland suburbs.

* Two other races featuring progressives in California have yet to be called. **Mai Vang** , a progressive from the Sacramento area, trails incumbent **Doris Matsui** by 15 points with less than half of the vote counted. **Aisha Wahab** , a progressive who won a special election to fill the northern California seat vacated by **Eric Swalwell** , leads her opponent, **Melissa Hernandez,** by 13 points, with just over half of the votes counted.
* **Nithya Raman** , whose Los Angeles City Council campaigns were boosted by the local D.S.A. chapter, [defeated](https://substack.com/redirect/82d4f514-d032-48ff-9b0d-76c166c59b9c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) incumbent Mayor **Karen Bass** in a contentious race. Raman maintains that she was an early advocate for a ceasefire in Gaza, and has characterized Israel's conduct in Gaza as a genocide. The national D.S.A. narrowly voted against rescinding the Los Angeles chapter's endorsement.
* **Civil-society groups propose delaying fight over Iran war until 2027:** A draft letter circulating among civil-society organizations, a copy of which was obtained by Drop Site Daily, initially proposed punting on the critical fight over war funding until 2027. After Drop Site approached the groups who had signed, the letter was adjusted to be more forceful. The background: Funding for the government expires on December 11, 2026. [Sen. ](https://substack.com/redirect/8f161ed9-9a35-435f-80a5-561f9cfe2bb8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[Chris Van Hollen](https://substack.com/redirect/8f161ed9-9a35-435f-80a5-561f9cfe2bb8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/8f161ed9-9a35-435f-80a5-561f9cfe2bb8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)and Rep. **Ro Khanna** have proposed using that date as leverage to force an end to the war, not through a war powers resolution--which Trump has already ignored--but by legally barring the government from spending money on the war. Instead, the groups signing the letter proposed focusing on measures that have no bearing on the administration's ability to prosecute the war. The letter read:
* "In Tuesday's elections, people across the United States made their will resoundingly clear: they want to end President Trump's war on Iran, its resulting violence, and its downstream economic hardship, immediately. Ending this war cannot wait."
* "We, the XX undersigned civil society organizations, urge you to respond to this mandate _by voting down any defense authorization or defense appropriations bills that would continue funding this disastrous war or increase Pentagon funding beyond the already outrageous $1 trillion_ that the White House pushed through Congress last year" (emphasis added).
* _But:_**** Congress has no plans to fund the war through a defense appropriations bill. The plan is to pass a continuing resolution on or before December 11. So far, signatories to the draft letter include the Center for International Policy Advocacy, Indivisible, J Street, MoveOn, National Iranian American Council Action, and Win Without War. The letter went on: "_If Trump continues the war into the new year, we further urge returning members to prioritize and pass legislation expressly defunding this war early in the new Congress._ " Such an approach would let Trump have November and December to wage war before _" expressly defunding this war early in the new Congress."_**** That line is being stripped out, sources said.
* **Matt Duss** , executive director of CIPA, one of the signatories, emphasized his support for the more aggressive approach proposed by Van Hollen. "Congress needs to use every tool it has right now to stop this war," he said. "We want everyone to be going all the way."
* At issue is the question of just how hard Democrats should fight Trump's war. Not every group involved, sources said, was yet convinced to take the approach called for by Duss and Van Hollen, despite the resounding mandate.

# Other International News
* **WHO approves Ebola vaccine trials for dangerous Bundibugyo strain:** On Monday, the World Health Organization [recommended](https://substack.com/redirect/ba742c5f-fde6-4575-a65f-bbbec75deecc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) two trials for Ebola vaccines that target the Bundibugyo strain. They will be tested in a trial led by the Democratic Republic of the Congo's National Institute for Biomedical Research. Trial results are expected by early 2027.

Ethiopia accuses Sudan of backing the Tigrayan rebels who launched an offensive against Ethiopian forces in September.
* **Workers strike and march across France:** Labor unions in France [called](https://substack.com/redirect/209511d4-1b22-4dd2-9f9d-61155aaeaf82?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a strike on Thursday to demand a higher minimum wage, higher salaries for all workers, tax reforms, and better school conditions. Security forces have already begun brutalizing protesters: In Lyon, riot police fired tear gas at a demonstration, Reuters reported.
* **Russian and Ukraine exchange attacks; Russia kills four civilians in Donetsk:** Russian attacks killed four civilians and injured five others in Donetsk on Wednesday, Al Jazeera [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/10758447-fe6f-448e-b2a0-b94ca6cc251a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and drones caused large fires at a logistics center in Bucha outside Kyiv district. More than 80 Russian drones hit Odesa, injuring six people, including a child, according to Ukrainian officials. Ukraine launched over 200 drone attacks on Russia's Ryazan region overnight, Russian officials said. The strikes injured one person, caused fires at sites including an oil refinery, and left areas without power.
* **Syria secures $400+ million Saudi loan in new defense agreement:** On Wednesday, the defense ministries of Saudi Arabia and Syria [signed](https://substack.com/redirect/d49de858-6090-4f9b-a631-780d38048dc0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a new agreement that will give Syria more than $403 million in Saudi loans for energy, housing, and infrastructure projects.
