The Saudi Fund for Development agreed to six concessional loans: $100 million for healthcare facilities; $60 million for housing; $105 million for civil defense; $90 million for the Aleppo thermal power plant; and $30 million for drinking water in Damascus and Idlib. The deal comes just days after the Syrian foreign minister, Asaad al-Shaibani, said that Syria may join the Saudi-Turkey-Pakistan "Mecca alliance."
* **Stabbing attack outside Sri Lanka embassy in Jordan kills security officer:** An assailant stabbed and [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/c394deb6-36b0-484d-b83a-bfe9c5f1fdcc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) an officer outside the Sri Lankan embassy in Amman on Thursday. In its preliminary investigation, Jordan's Public Security Directorate said that the attacker had planned "to commit the terrorist act against the officers of the General Security Directorate." The attacker was previously convicted of joining "terrorist groups," according to court filings, and of conspiring to carry out attacks in Jordan.
* **Colombia expected to pass law toughening terms of surrender for armed group, breaking with "total peace" policy: **Colombia's Congress [passed](https://substack.com/redirect/f7b9831c-331a-4ee6-9561-f94cd9a1e8dc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a bill that increases the scope of punishments for militants who lay down their arms. The right-wing President Abelardo De La Espriella, who shepherded its passage, is expected to sign the bill into law. The legislation bars surrendering militants from holding elected office or entering peace negotiations. It would put conditions on the length of their prison sentences. In exchange for reducing their sentences by up to 50%, they must disarm, identify fellow militants, hand over recruited and kidnapped minors, help search for the missing, surrender their assets, and disclose their political and corruption networks. If it becomes law, the measures would represent a radical divergence the "total peace policy" put in place by the left-wing former president, Gustavo Petro. That policy, which began in 2024, allowed for Colombia's government to negotiate directly with the country's armed and criminal groups.
* **UN elects five judges to International Court of Justice:** On Tuesday, the UN [elected](https://substack.com/redirect/049ca713-8a5a-4ef6-8d98-076a843fba13?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) five new judges to the International Court of Justice:**** Dapo Akande of the United Kingdom; Francois Alabrune of France; Mahmoud Daifallah Hmoud of Jordan; Rena Lee of Singapore; and Phoebe Okowa of Kenya. The UN General Assembly and the Security Council initially agreed on all but one of the candidates: Okowa of Kenya, who faced a challenge from the Ecuadoran diplomat and jurist Marcelo Vazquez-Bermudez. ICJ President Yuji Iwasawa said that 24 legal cases are pending at the court, including South Africa's genocide case against Israel for its war in Gaza. Iwasawa said that the court will deliver its judgment in The Gambia's genocide case against Myanmar on November 19.
* **Bomb threats disrupt European air travel:** Bomb threats disrupted commercial flights throughout Europe Thursday, resulting in emergency landings and some military escorts for airplanes. A threat targeting flights to Rome was sent via email from a group describing itself as "anti-feminist," the AP [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/f22c583b-d793-42ce-89c2-9c067cfbad07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), saying that at least one other airport received a similar message. The disruptions follow a series of other bomb threats in Europe earlier this week.

Drop Site Daily: November 5, 2026 | | | Nov 5 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- U.S. President Donald Trump watches as the last piece of steel is hoisted for construction of the White House ballroom on November 4, 2026 in Washington, DC. Photo by Andrew Harnik/Getty Images. Thursday, November 5, 2026 -** Iran: Vice President JD Vance blames Republican election losses on Iran war; Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf accuses U.S. of putting Israel first. Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei says U.S. midterm results will not change Washington's hostility toward Tehran. Iran says two tankers, tugboat catch fire in Strait of Hormuz; UK reports tanker attacked near Qatar. South Korea plans to expand naval mission near Strait of Hormuz. U.S. sanctions Indian, Turkish firms over alleged ties to Iranian oil, aviation. UAE airline profits plunge 66% amid Iran war. Palestine: Israeli attacks kill three Palestinians, including child, in Gaza. Israeli settlers seize homes near Jericho, expelling Palestinians; settlers say they are "dismantling the Oslo Accords." Israel demolishes five buildings, displacing 105 Palestinians, and shuts down club in occupied East Jerusalem. Israeli settlers burn olive trees, assault Palestinians as soldiers demolish homes across the West Bank. Yemen: Saudi-led strikes kill around 20 across Yemen; Ansarallah shelling kills woman, wounds five in Taiz. WSJ: Ansarallah demands recognition of sovereignty over Yemen, $51 billion in compensation in exchange for halting attacks on Saudi Arabia. Lebanon: Israeli strike kills one in southern Lebanon, again violating ceasefire. Lebanon issues arrest warrants for two Hezbollah members over seized explosives. U.S.: Democrats extend power in House, state races in latest midterm election results. Exclusive: Civil-society groups propose delaying fight over Iran war until 2027. CBS: Trump asks advisers if he should remove War Secretary Pete Hegseth. NYT: SCOTUS justice Samuel Alito privately says he won't retire immediately, despite Democrats' Senate win. House Speaker Mike Johnson will not seek leadership role. Billionaire Leon Black sues Rep. Robert Garcia for defamation over remarks about Epstein ties. International: World Health Organization approves Ebola vaccine trials for dangerous Bundibugyo strain. Sudanese Army strike in North Kordofan kills two women, destroys water station. Ethiopia, Sudan close each other's consulates. Workers strike and march across France. Russian and Ukraine exchange attacks; Russia kills four civilians in Donetsk. Syria secures $400+ million Saudi loan in new defense agreement. Stabbing attack outside Sri Lanka embassy in Jordan kills security officer. Colombia expected to pass law toughening terms of surrender for armed group, breaking with "total peace" policy. UN elects five judges to International Court of Justice. Bomb threats disrupt European air travel. This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Iran Vance blames Republican election losses on Iran war; Iran 's Ghalibaf accuses U.S. of putting Israel first: The Iran war was the main reason Republicans lost the 2026 midterm elections, U.S. Vice President JD Vance on Thursday, arguing that voters who backed President Donald Trump in 2024 switched to supporting Democrats despite strong Republican turnout. Citing private polling that he said accurately anticipated the results, Vance identified four leading reasons former Trump voters abandoned Republicans: "End the war," "Focus on cost of living/inflation," "Put America First," and "Change our relationship to Israel." He said the findings vindicated calls for a diplomatic resolution to the conflict, and he warned against attributing the losses to the Trump administration's far-right immigration policies. "The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night," Vance wrote. "If you'd like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so." Responding to Vance, Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf the Trump administration of preparing another phase of the conflict while prioritizing Israel over American interests. "Boss is prepping the next war phase while America teeters on an Israel-First cliff," Ghalibaf wrote, adding: "Why not say this to your boss?" Iran 's Khamenei says U.S. midterm results will not change Washington's hostility toward Tehran: Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei said on Wednesday that anyone expecting a change in U.S. policy following Republican losses in the midterm elections is "seriously mistaken." "Those who still harbor even the slightest hope that the behavior of the hegemonic system might change through partisan or factional shifts . . . are seriously mistaken," Khamenei said in a written statement published on his website. Iran says two tankers, tugboat catch fire in Strait of Hormuz; UK reports tanker attacked near Qatar: Two oil tankers in separate incidents in the Strait of Hormuz after attempting to use "unauthorized" shipping routes, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy said on Thursday. A tugboat attempting to extinguish the fire also caught fire. A tanker was struck by two unidentified projectiles approximately 50 nautical miles north of Madinat Al-Shamal, Qatar, the UK Maritime Trade Operations reported on Thursday. The condition of the crew and the extent of damage remain unconfirmed. South Korea plans to expand naval mission near Strait of Hormuz: South Korea to expand its anti-piracy naval mission in the Gulf of Aden toward waters south of Oman, near the Strait of Hormuz, and deploy additional military assets, Yonhap reported on Thursday. It would be Seoul's first military contribution to maritime security efforts in the region since the U.S.-Iran war began in February. In September, South Korea declined U.S. requests for direct military support against Tehran. South Korean defense officials stressed that the mission would not involve combat forces and would remain independent of allied military operations. They said that aircraft will be prohibited from monitoring Iranian territory or entering the Strait of Hormuz. U.S. sanctions Indian, Turkish firms over alleged ties to Iranian oil, aviation: On Wednesday, the U.S. Treasury Department sanctions on individuals and companies in India and Turkey over their alleged support for Iran's oil and aviation sectors, as part of the Trump administration's Operation Economic Outcast campaign to restrict Iranian oil revenues during the war. The Treasury Department accused Indian entities of falsifying vessel registrations for ships transporting Iranian oil. It also sanctioned Turkey-based Fugo Ground Services Inc. for supporting Iran's aviation sector. The Treasury Department said last week that its sanctions campaign had contributed to the collapse of Iran's currency and increased inflation almost 90%. UAE airline profits plunge 66% amid Iran war: The Dubai-based Emirates Group airline sustained a 66% decline in its after-tax profits, it on Thursday. Year-on-year, the airline's profit fell to $1 billion in the first half of its 2026-27 financial year, as the Iran war disrupted air travel and pushed up fuel costs. The Emirates airline carried 21.8 million passengers between April and September, down 22% from a year earlier. The company said that it remained profitable despite the disruptions, with cash reserves declining to $14.7 billion by the end of September. Palestine Israeli attacks kill three Palestinians, including child, in Gaza: Israeli forces a woman in Al-Mawasi, west of Khan Younis in southern Gaza, and a child in the Bureij refugee camp in central Gaza on Thursday, WAFA reported. Another Palestinian was killed in an Israeli airstrike west of Al-Zawayda in central Gaza. Israeli settlers seize homes near Jericho, expelling Palestinians; settlers say they are "dismantling the Oslo Accords": Around 30 Israeli settlers, some of whom were armed, eight homes in Ein Al-Duyuk Al-Tahta on the outskirts of Jericho in the occupied West Bank on Wednesday. Activists warned that settlers could be reproducing the situation in Hebron, where armed Israeli settlers live in enclaves inside the Palestinian city, contributing to displacement and severe restrictions on Palestinian freedom of mobility. The operation near Jericho was organized by the Nachala settlement movement, which claims to have secretly purchased the properties. Sixty-five Palestinian residents fled after settlers attacked them with stones, an activist the Times of Israel. Residents said that Israeli forces subsequently blocked access to the area, leaving homeowners afraid to return. The new outpost is reportedly located in Area C, under full Israeli control under the Oslo Accords, just meters from parts of Jericho classified as Area A, where the Palestinian Authority is supposed to exercise civilian and security control. Yisrael Gantz, head of the West Bank settler council, framed the move as an effort to dismantle the Oslo Accords, declaring: "Today we begin reversing the trend, dismantling the Oslo Accords through actions, house by house, family by family." Palestinian National Council Speaker Rawhi Fattouh condemned the takeover as "organized terrorism" carried out under Israeli government protection, charging Israel of encouraging settlement expansion and forced displacement. Israel demolishes five buildings, displacing 105 Palestinians, and shuts down club in occupied East Jerusalem: Israeli forces five residential buildings containing 12 apartments in the town of Biddu, northwest of occupied East Jerusalem, on Thursday, displacing 105 Palestinians without prior warning, citing construction without permits. Soldiers fired stun grenades and tear gas at residents and prevented families from removing their belongings before demolishing their homes, according to the Jerusalem Governorate. Separately, Israeli authorities shut down the Abna Al-Quds Club in Jerusalem's Old City under an order issued by National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir. The governorate condemned both measures as part of an escalating Israeli campaign targeting Palestinian homes, institutions, and community life in Jerusalem. Israeli settlers burn olive trees, assault Palestinians as soldiers demolish homes across the West Bank: Ramallah: Israeli settlers to dozens of centuries-old olive trees in the village of Burqa, east of Ramallah, on Thursday, according to WAFA. Jericho: Three Palestinians were after settlers, accompanied by Israeli forces, raided Palestinian homes in the Bedouin communities of Ard Satih, west of Jericho, beating residents and spraying them with pepper spray. Nablus: Settlers farmers in Beita, south of Nablus, injuring one Palestinian. Israeli forces also demolished a home in Furush Beit Dajan, east of Nablus. Salfit: Israeli forces a home in Qarawat Bani Hassan and issued a stop-work order for another home. Three Palestinians were also injured in assaults by Israeli soldiers and settlers in the town. Yemen Saudi-led strikes kill around 20 across Yemen; Ansarallah shelling kills woman, wounds five in Taiz: Saudi-led coalition bombardment killed around 20 people across the Yemeni governorates of Al-Jawf, Al-Bayda, Saada, and Taiz over the past 24 hours, according to Ansarallah-affiliated media. Ansarallah military spokesman Yahya Saree said that the coalition carried out 104 attacks across areas controlled by the group, including the capital, Sana'a. Meanwhile, Yemen's Saudi-backed government reported that Ansarallah shelling in Taiz killed a woman and wounded five people. WSJ: Ansarallah demands recognition of sovereignty over Yemen, $51 billion in compensation in exchange for halting attacks on Saudi Arabia: Yemen's Ansarallah $51 billion in compensation for years of Saudi airstrikes and blockade and formal recognition as Yemen's sovereign power in exchange for halting attacks on Saudi Arabia, the Wall Street Journal reported. Riyadh reportedly approached the group after Ansarallah attacks on Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea and territorial advances near the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait. Saudi officials told the WSJ that Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman is reluctant to negotiate without military leverage but fears that deploying additional ground troops could result in heavy casualties. The UAE's withdrawal from the anti-Ansarallah campaign, Washington's refusal to provide direct military support, and Saudi's reliance on regional allies further complicated Riyadh's options, the report said. Lebanon Israeli strike kills one in southern Lebanon, again violating ceasefire: An Israeli drone strike killed one person and wounded another in Qabrikha, in the Marjeyoun district of southern Lebanon, on Wednesday, Lebanon's National News Agency reported. The Israeli military that it targeted two people who were "observing" its forces in the area, without providing any evidence that the individuals were military targets. Separately, Israeli warplanes two airstrikes on Tallousa and its outskirts in the Marjeyoun district, and struck the outskirts of Aita al-Jabal in the Bint Jbeil district. Lebanon issues arrest warrants for two Hezbollah members over seized explosives: Lebanon's Military Court issued arrest warrants for two Hezbollah members in connection with the seizure of 780 kilograms (1,720 pounds) of explosives at the Dahr Al-Baydar checkpoint linking Beirut to the Bekaa Valley, the National News Agency reported. The explosives were seized last month. Lebanese authorities indicted 13 people in the case, on charges involving state security, illegal possession of weapons and explosives, and forming unlawful organizations. Beyond the two Hezbollah members, the remaining 11 defendants are still at large. The government's attempt to question six defendants was postponed following an objection filed by their lawyer. U.S. News Democrats extend power in House, state races in latest midterm election results: Additional races were called on Wednesday, extending Democrats' commanding lead in the House of Representatives and in state-level posts. Senate elections in Mississippi and Alaska remain uncalled as of Thursday morning, while an unexpectedly tight Senate race in Louisiana was called in favor of the Republican, Julia Letlow. Sam Forstag, a labor union leader and smokejumper endorsed by Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez , won his election to represent Montana's first congressional district, a seat previously held by Trump's former Interior Secretary, Ryan Zinke. Forstag is the first Democratic candidate to win a congressional race in the state since former Sen. Jon Tester won in 2018. He is also the youngest congressional representative from the state since the 1930s. Progressive activist William Lawrence officially Republican incumbent Tom Barrett in Michigan's seventh congressional district. Lawrence, a co-founder of the Sunrise Movement, won one of the most competitive elections this cycle by emphasizing the rising cost of living in Michigan, opposing data centers, calling for restrictions on Flock cameras, and pushing for tighter regulation of artificial intelligence. Republican incumbent Rep. Max Miller , who was accused of physical and verbal abuse by his ex-wife, conceded defeat to Democrat Brian Poindexter in Ohio's seventh congressional district, which covers much of the Cleveland suburbs. Progressive Angela Gonzales-Torres defeated incumbent Democrat Rep. Jimmy Gomez in California's 34th congressional district. The 31-year-old was backed by Justice Democrats and the Los Angeles chapter of the Democratic Socialists of America in her May primary against the AIPAC-backed Gomez. Two other races featuring progressives in California have yet to be called. Mai Vang , a progressive from the Sacramento area, trails incumbent Doris Matsui by 15 points with less than half of the vote counted. Aisha Wahab , a progressive who won a special election to fill the northern California seat vacated by Eric Swalwell , leads her opponent, Melissa Hernandez, by 13 points, with just over half of the votes counted. Nithya Raman , whose Los Angeles City Council campaigns were boosted by the local D.S.A. chapter, incumbent Mayor Karen Bass in a contentious race. Los Angeles's D.S.A. chapter endorsed her candidacy for mayor, despite Raman's acceptance of an endorsement from a pro-Israel group and lack of clarity on whether she supports the Boycott, Divestment, Sanctions movement. Raman maintains that she was an early advocate for a ceasefire in Gaza, and has characterized Israel's conduct in Gaza as a genocide. The national D.S.A. narrowly voted against rescinding the Los Angeles chapter's endorsement. Civil-society groups propose delaying fight over Iran war until 2027: A draft letter circulating among civil-society organizations, a copy of which was obtained by Drop Site Daily, initially proposed punting on the critical fight over war funding until 2027. After Drop Site approached the groups who had signed, the letter was adjusted to be more forceful. The background: Funding for the government expires on December 11, 2026. Rep. Ro Khanna have proposed using that date as leverage to force an end to the war, not through a war powers resolution--which Trump has already ignored--but by legally barring the government from spending money on the war. Instead, the groups signing the letter proposed focusing on measures that have no bearing on the administration's ability to prosecute the war. The letter read: "In Tuesday's elections, people across the United States made their will resoundingly clear: they want to end President Trump's war on Iran, its resulting violence, and its downstream economic hardship, immediately. Ending this war cannot wait." "We, the XX undersigned civil society organizations, urge you to respond to this mandate by voting down any defense authorization or defense appropriations bills that would continue funding this disastrous war or increase Pentagon funding beyond the already outrageous $1 trillion that the White House pushed through Congress last year" (emphasis added). But: Congress has no plans to fund the war through a defense appropriations bill. The plan is to pass a continuing resolution on or before December 11. So far, signatories to the draft letter include the Center for International Policy Advocacy, Indivisible, J Street, MoveOn, National Iranian American Council Action, and Win Without War. The letter went on: "If Trump continues the war into the new year, we further urge returning members to prioritize and pass legislation expressly defunding this war early in the new Congress. " Such an approach would let Trump have November and December to wage war before " expressly defunding this war early in the new Congress." That line is being stripped out, sources said. Matt Duss , executive director of CIPA, one of the signatories, emphasized his support for the more aggressive approach proposed by Van Hollen. "Congress needs to use every tool it has right now to stop this war," he said. "We want everyone to be going all the way." At issue is the question of just how hard Democrats should fight Trump's war. Not every group involved, sources said, was yet convinced to take the approach called for by Duss and Van Hollen, despite the resounding mandate. CBS: Trump asks advisers if he should remove War Secretary Pete Hegseth: Trump is his advisers if he should remove War Secretary Pete Hegseth from his post, CBS News reported on Wednesday, suggesting that the president is searching for a scapegoat after the Republican Party suffered historic election losses driven by voter anger over the Iran war. Some aides predict that blame will fall on U.S. military Commander Adm. Brad Cooper , the head of Central Command, and the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, Gen. Dan Caine. Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis is being floated as a replacement for Hegseth. If Hegseth is replaced, he may try to take up the Tennessee Senate seat that Marsha Blackburn is vacating to become governor. Trump has told reporters that Hegseth would be "very popular" as a senator. NYT: SCOTUS justice Samuel Alito privately says he won 't retire immediately, despite Democrats' Senate win: The Supreme Court Justice Samuel Alito privately says he intends to remain on the bench after Democrats swept the Senate, two people close to Alito the New York Times. His announcement follows speculation that he or Justice Clarence Thomas might retire during the lame-duck session. Some experts speculate that outgoing Republican senators--such as John Cornyn, Bill Cassidy, or Susan Collins--might try to help Trump push a new SCOTUS nominee through the confirmation process. House Speaker Mike Johnson will not seek leadership role: Following the Democratic takeover of the House of Representatives, SpeakerMike Johnson told staff on Wednesday he will not the minority leader post in the new Congress. After the news broke, House Majority Leader Steve Scalise a "consensus-driven" bid for the Minority Leader position, saying that the election "was far worse than any of us expected." He will Judiciary Chairman Jim Jordan , who also announced a bid to become House Minority Leader on Wednesday, touting his "battle-testing" in oversight hearings and his readiness to counter Democratic investigations. Republicans will vote for new leadership on November 10. Rep. Tom Emmer(R-Minn.), the current Majority Whip and the presumptive Minority Whip, a challenge from Rep. August Pfluger(R-Texas), ABC News reported on Wednesday. Emmer told colleagues in a letter that he took Tuesday's failures "personally" and could not "sugarcoat" Republican defeats. Pfluger, for his part, promoted his ability to make "the changes" the caucus would need to win in 2028. Billionaire Leon Black sues Rep. Robert Garcia for defamation over remarks about Epstein ties: Private equity magnate Leon Black a lawsuit in New York federal court on Wednesday, claiming that California congressman Robert Garcia defamed him for saying that Black was among the last people to interact with Jeffrey Epstein before his death, and that victims credibly named Black as involved in abuse. Black acknowledges knowing Epstein and paying him $158 million for tax and estate planning, but he denies knowledge of Epstein's crimes and says that he cut ties with Epstein in 2018. Black said that Garcia's statements cost him investment opportunities and $775,000 in private security, and accuses Garcia of seeking political benefit from public anger over Epstein. In September, the House of Representatives held Black in contempt for ignoring subpoenas from the Oversight Committee about possible nondisclosure agreements with women tied to Epstein. Black has sued the committee, arguing that the subpoenas were invalid. Garcia has vowed to pursue the Epstein investigation. He is expected to head the House Oversight Committee in the new Congress. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News WHO approves Ebola vaccine trials for dangerous Bundibugyo strain: On Monday, the World Health Organization two trials for Ebola vaccines that target the Bundibugyo strain. The strain has killed more than 5,300 people since May, with a fatality rate of about 50%. Currently, there is no strain-specific vaccine or treatment available. The new vaccines are being jointly developed by the University of Oxford, the Serum Institute of India, and Moderna, WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said. They will be tested in a trial led by the Democratic Republic of the Congo's National Institute for Biomedical Research. Trial results are expected by early 2027. Sudanese Army strike in North Kordofan kills two women, destroys water station: The Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) a neighborhood in the Um Badr area of North Kordofan, killing two women and injuring 10 other people, the Sudan Tribune reported. The same wave of airstrikes hit the Al-Kabjark water station at Khor Dardaq, destroying tanks, pumps, and solar panels at a vital water facility for residents. Ethiopia, Sudan close each other 's consulates: On Wednesday, Ethiopia the Sudanese consulate in Assosa and ordered Sudanese diplomats to leave, Reuters reported. Sudan then closed the Ethiopian consulate in Gedaref and expelled Ethiopian diplomats. Sudan accuses Ethiopia of supporting the Rapid Support Forces and allowing the RSF to launch drone strikes from Ethiopian territory. Ethiopia accuses Sudan of backing the Tigrayan rebels who launched an offensive against Ethiopian forces in September. Workers strike and march across France: Labor unions in France a strike on Thursday to demand a higher minimum wage, higher salaries for all workers, tax reforms, and better school conditions. Protests are planned in 260 cities and towns, and the Education Ministry expects 16% of the country's public-school teachers to strike. President Emmanuel Macron convened a meeting with his defense and security advisers on Wednesday to "ensure public order." Security forces have already begun brutalizing protesters: In Lyon, riot police fired tear gas at a demonstration, Reuters reported. Russian and Ukraine exchange attacks; Russia kills four civilians in Donetsk: Russian attacks killed four civilians and injured five others in Donetsk on Wednesday, Al Jazeera , and drones caused large fires at a logistics center in Bucha outside Kyiv district. Russian forces also attacked a postal terminal near Kharkiv, a power substation in Dnipropetrovsk, and a dry cargo ship carrying military equipment near Odesa, its Defense Ministry said on Thursday. More than 80 Russian drones hit Odesa, injuring six people, including a child, according to Ukrainian officials. Ukraine launched over 200 drone attacks on Russia's Ryazan region overnight, Russian officials said. The strikes injured one person, caused fires at sites including an oil refinery, and left areas without power. Syria secures $400+ million Saudi loan in new defense agreement: On Wednesday, the defense ministries of Saudi Arabia and Syria a new agreement that will give Syria more than $403 million in Saudi loans for energy, housing, and infrastructure projects. The terms of the agreement have not been disclosed. The Saudi Fund for Development agreed to six concessional loans: $100 million for healthcare facilities; $60 million for housing; $105 million for civil defense; $90 million for the Aleppo thermal power plant; and $30 million for drinking water in Damascus and Idlib. The deal comes just days after the Syrian foreign minister, Asaad al-Shaibani, said that Syria may join the Saudi-Turkey-Pakistan "Mecca alliance." Stabbing attack outside Sri Lanka embassy in Jordan kills security officer: An assailant stabbed and an officer outside the Sri Lankan embassy in Amman on Thursday. The attacker reportedly tried to seize a guard's weapon before he was subdued. He sustained injuries and is in critical condition. The attack injured a second officer, who is being hospitalized. In its preliminary investigation, Jordan's Public Security Directorate said that the attacker had planned "to commit the terrorist act against the officers of the General Security Directorate." The attacker was previously convicted of joining "terrorist groups," according to court filings, and of conspiring to carry out attacks in Jordan. Colombia expected to pass law toughening terms of surrender for armed group, breaking with "total peace" policy: Colombia's Congress a bill that increases the scope of punishments for militants who lay down their arms. The right-wing President Abelardo De La Espriella, who shepherded its passage, is expected to sign the bill into law. The legislation bars surrendering militants from holding elected office or entering peace negotiations. It would put conditions on the length of their prison sentences. In exchange for reducing their sentences by up to 50%, they must disarm, identify fellow militants, hand over recruited and kidnapped minors, help search for the missing, surrender their assets, and disclose their political and corruption networks. If it becomes law, the measures would represent a radical divergence the "total peace policy" put in place by the left-wing former president, Gustavo Petro. That policy, which began in 2024, allowed for Colombia's government to negotiate directly with the country's armed and criminal groups. UN elects five judges to International Court of Justice: On Tuesday, the UN five new judges to the International Court of Justice:** Dapo Akande of the United Kingdom; Francois Alabrune of France; Mahmoud Daifallah Hmoud of Jordan; Rena Lee of Singapore; and Phoebe Okowa of Kenya. They will join the bench in February 2027. The UN General Assembly and the Security Council initially agreed on all but one of the candidates: Okowa of Kenya, who faced a challenge from the Ecuadoran diplomat and jurist Marcelo Vazquez-Bermudez. ICJ President Yuji Iwasawa said that 24 legal cases are pending at the court, including South Africa's genocide case against Israel for its war in Gaza. Iwasawa said that the court will deliver its judgment in The Gambia's genocide case against Myanmar on November 19. Bomb threats disrupt European air travel: Bomb threats disrupted commercial flights throughout Europe Thursday, resulting in emergency landings and some military escorts for airplanes. A threat targeting flights to Rome was sent via email from a group describing itself as "anti-feminist," the AP , saying that at least one other airport received a similar message. On election night, Donald Trump became what _every_ two-term president eventually becomes: a divided-government president. Democrats won the House and the Senate in the same night, and they did it with margins that should retire the phrase "a historic midterm correction" from every talking head's mouth in America.
Let's put the numbers on the actual historical ledger, because the comparison is the whole argument:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/73df1355-00dd-4a44-9886-a1b9701e4a03?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
2026: Democrats netted roughly 27 to 31 House seats -- and that's after Republicans redrew Texas and Florida to hand themselves nine extra seats. The final House count is heading toward 250-plus Democratic seats, their largest majority since the early 2010s. In the Senate, Democrats flipped at least seven seats -- Iowa, Kansas, Maine, North Carolina, Ohio, South Carolina, and Texas, with Alaska and Mississippi still counting -- for a 54-47 majority, possibly 55-56\. That is _half the Obama 'shellacking'_. And five governorships flipped: Georgia, Iowa, Nevada, Ohio, and Texas. Democrats now hold _more governorships_ than at any moment since before 2010.
The honest historical analog, is not 1982. It's Obama 2006 -- a minus-30 House night that cost the Democrats both chambers. Except this one happened on a map Republicans personally gerrymandered to prevent exactly this outcome. They flipped a handful of majority-black Democratic seats in the South and still lost everything that mattered. The AP's voter polling gives the autopsy: inflation that got _worse_ , not better, the Iran war, immigration, and a corruption smell that wouldn't wash off.
Trump's own response -- "I can work with Dems on many more things than people understand" -- is pure Truman-after-1946. Fine. But here is what should frighten movement conservatives far more than a lost Capitol: **the states AKA heartland**.
**Two revolutions, same night**
Look at the personnel list, because it tells you where the energy actually is.
In the deep-blue cities, the left didn't just win -- it consolidated. Zohran Mamdani took New York City last year. This month, DSA member Nithya Raman ended Karen Bass's mayoralty in Los Angeles, becoming the first Asian American mayor in that city's history. In San Francisco, Scott Wiener crushed Nancy Pelosi's own endorsed candidate, 55 to 45, for the seat Pelosi held for four decades. New York sent a DSA-backed slate to the House -- Brad Lander, Claire Valdez, Darializa Avila Chevalier -- alongside AOC and presumptive next Speaker Jeffries. Kentucky elected its first socialist state legislator since the 1800s. There are now a record seven Muslim Americans in Congress, including the first Muslim US senator, and at least 36 winners nationwide at every level of government. In Michigan, Abdul El-Sayed carried Dearborn by 65 points on the _biggest turnout in that city 's recorded history_.
To be precise -- and precision matters if you want to win -- several of these wins are more complicated than the horror-show version. Wiener is a YIMBY progressive who beat the machine, not a DSA member. El-Sayed calls himself a capitalist. The socialist wave, as Brookings put it, showed "gains but limited reach": almost all of it inside safe blue seats. But that's actually the worse diagnosis, not the better one. You can beat an ideologue with a well-funded moderate. What you cannot beat is an organized, multi-cycle, city-level machine that treats school boards, state houses, and congressional seats as one continuous ladder. Funded from out of state. That machine now exists on the American left, it just ran its most successful election in history, and it has a farm system the right simply does not have.
**The states are the emergency**
Because here's the part of the night that got lost under CNN and MSNOWs 'the DC wreckage: **the same electorate that did this also flipped Texas**.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9f4ac0bc-597e-40d2-952c-dd1068ea0b43?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
2,848 of 3,109 counties moved toward Democrats
Gina Hinojosa unseated Greg Abbott. Talarico took the Senate seat. Democrats broke a Republican trifecta in the Texas House that had stood since 2003. Republicans kept the state Senate by a thread. And the mechanism wasn't mysterious -- the Texas Tribune's county data shows _border_ _counties_ that went R+16 and R+22 for Trump in 2024 swinging to D+56 and D+41 in 2026, on record Latino turnout and a massive expansion of the electorate, especially young voters. That is what an erosion looks like in real time. If it's turnout, it's fixable. If it's realignment, Texas 2028 is gone and the Electoral College is effectively gone with it. Nobody in Texas Republican politics currently knows which one it is -- and _the party has about 24 months to find out_.
Then there's the governance record, which is where "cleaned up" stops being a slogan and becomes a to-do list. Minnesota is the case study every state should be forced to read: 78 people charged, 57 convicted in the Feeding Our Future orbit, fourteen separate Medicaid-funded programs under federal and state investigation, federal child-care money frozen outright. And note the detail that blows up the comfortable version of the story: the Columbus, Ohio daycare allegations broke under a Republican governor. This is not a blue-state disease and not an immigration story -- it is a _program-oversight failure_ that happens wherever nobody audits the vendors. Every state in the union passes through federal money with 2010-era verification behind it. "Clean up the programs" is a governing agenda that polls in every swing state without a single culture-war word attached. This is why Marsha Blackburn's first presser after winning Tennessee Governor mentioned a DOGE for her state to begin during her transition period.
Republicans have two years of divided government in DC to pass nothing -- so the statehouse agenda is the only agenda.
And the two-year clock is real. The first tests of the post-2026 Republican Party arrive in 2027, in the off-year governor's races in Kentucky, Louisiana, and Mississippi -- Jeff Landry's own race in Baton Rouge becomes the opening referendum on whether the party can hold what it has, or whether the 2026 tide was the start of something. Then comes 2028, the last election cycle before the **2030 Census** redraws every map in the country. Will it be citizens only or like 2020 headcount? Lose the states through 2028 and the next decade is drawn for you.
**The verdict**
DC is already broken, Speaker Johnson and Leader Thune didn't help -- and 2026 made it worse than any midterm in modern memory for a Republican president, worse than 2010 in the Senate, worse than 2006 in consequence, on a map built to make it milder. Trump will spend 2027 vetoing things and calling it strategy. Fine.
But DC was always going to be lost in a sixth-year-type environment. The states are where the loss becomes _permanent_ or gets _reversed_ -- and the **heartland** is exactly where the other side just built its deepest bench, its strongest turnout machine, and its cleanest governing argument. Two years. Three governor's races in 2027. One census after that.
Clean up the states, or the states clean up the map -- and keep it.

#### **[When Democrats lost in 2024, I made a choice: get back to work. That's why I started Endless Urgency. We're building an independent media platform that tells the truth, holds the powerful accountable, and helps rebuild a Democratic Party that actually fights for people. If you believe in that mission, become a paid subscriber for just $8/month and help us build something that lasts:](https://substack.com/redirect/d7510169-f4f8-4222-a754-7446e275dc13?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

_Already a paid subscriber? Then like, share, and keep showing up in the comments. It matters more than you know._
* * *
Election night was amazing for so many reasons. Watching a new generation of Democratic leaders rise, Texas turning blue, and getting the chance to put one hand back on the wheel for sanity and decency in this country, was extraordinary.
But I'll be honest. There was something else I was enjoying, too: the total meltdown of MAGA influencers as they lose their grip on reality. They're being forced to accept that they're unpopular, and that they've spent the last two years destroying this country. A lot of them can't handle it.
Exhibit A, my old pal Laura Loomer. Conspiracy theorist, right-wing lunatic, deeply unwell human being. On Elon Musk's Twitter, she announced that America was over, that we're now an Islamic country, and basically threatened to leave.
That one has stuck with me, because I know what it feels like to lose.
When Democrats lost in 2024, when someone I have a great deal of respect for--Kamala Harris--lost, I didn't say America was over. I didn't threaten to leave. I didn't claim we'd been overrun by Nazis. I went back to work. I tried to figure out what I had done to contribute to this mess and what I could do differently over the next two years. Out of that came Endless Urgency and much of what I'm building right now to help rebuild the Democratic Party and fix this country.
Loomer isn't doing that. She's threatening to leave. Which, by the way, I'd support.
That's the message I sent her on Twitter, and I want to repeat it to all of you, because these people are disgustingly unpatriotic: You're free to leave.
The American people have spoken. Apparently they're the last institution in this country willing to stand up to Donald Trump and the Republican Party. MAGA doesn't like it. Fine. You can leave.
And that goes double for Laura Loomer, Tim Pool, Benny Johnson, and the rest of the MAGA influencer class, who are so very clearly taking money from foreign governments to pollute our politics and spread propaganda. Get the fuck out of our country. Go to whatever Middle Eastern nation has been paying your bills and go live there. Leave us the fuck alone.
And it isn't just the influencers. The craziness is everywhere.
I was on a right-wing show yesterday and suggested that Republicans lost because they've lost touch with reality. They spend too much time in their echo chambers and let crazy people run their campaigns, run for office, instead of qualified human beings who might actually know what the fuck they're doing.
* * *
#### **[Here's the difference between us and MAGA: when we lose, we organize. When they lose, they melt down. Endless Urgency exists because outrage alone isn't enough. We need to turn that energy into action, build our own media infrastructure, and fight for the future of this country every single day. Your paid subscription helps us expand our team, launch our content studio, and keep doing this work without answering to billionaires or corporate interests.](https://substack.com/redirect/d7510169-f4f8-4222-a754-7446e275dc13?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/d7510169-f4f8-4222-a754-7446e275dc13?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
A woman from Texas started screaming at me. James Talarico, she said, was going to steal my child and turn him trans. I hadn't even recovered from that when she explained the real reason Greg Abbott lost: he let too many Muslims into Texas.
That's where the Republican Party is right now. In 2025 there were a million think pieces about whether Democrats would learn the lesson of 2024: that we were too often focused on the wrong things instead of passing legislation and focusing on ways to make a material difference in your life. That's the lesson Republicans should be learning right now. Instead, they're doubling down on the same stupid shit. Loomer crashing out about America becoming Islamic and a woman screaming about Muslims in Texas aren't outliers. They are the party.
These people contribute nothing to society and nothing to public discourse except hate and lies. I hope someday they see the light and become more than the miserable human beings they are. I don't expect it.
Here's where the fun of election night ends. As much they'll threaten to leave, they're not going anywhere. There's a presidential election coming, and it will be a huge opportunity to make money and steal influence. JD Vance is already rebuilding the freak coalition for 2028. He won't fully condemn Nick Fuentes, who is basically a white supremacist, and he's back-channeling with Tucker Carlson to keep him out of the race.
They'll all make up and get back on the same page, because they hate Democrats, they hate liberal democracy, and they believe the American government is simply a piggy bank for corrupt billionaires like Donald Trump and Elon Musk, instead of the mechanism to improve your life.
So yes, enjoy this week. You earned it! But these people will remain a corrosive force in American politics until they're removed from it, or at least marginalized to the point that they have no meaningful influence. Democrats aren't perfect. But, we have a real chance to show people what good government looks like, and part of that job is taking these people on and exposing exactly what they're doing.
That doesn't happen on its own.
When they lose, they whine on the internet. They threaten to leave. They blame Muslims and trans kids and anyone but themselves.
When we lose, we go back to work the next morning. That's what I did in 2024, and it's what we'll keep doing until these people are gone from our politics.
With urgency,
--Mike

I didn't claim we'd been overrun by Nazis. I went back to work. I tried to figure out what I had done to contribute to this mess and what I could do differently over the next two years. Out of that came Endless Urgency and much of what I'm building right now to help rebuild the Democratic Party and fix this country. Loomer isn't doing that. She's threatening to leave. Which, by the way, I'd support. That's the message I sent her on Twitter, and I want to repeat it to all of you, because these people are disgustingly unpatriotic: You're free to leave. The American people have spoken. Apparently they're the last institution in this country willing to stand up to Donald Trump and the Republican Party. MAGA doesn't like it. Fine. You can leave. And that goes double for Laura Loomer, Tim Pool, Benny Johnson, and the rest of the MAGA influencer class, who are so very clearly taking money from foreign governments to pollute our politics and spread propaganda. Get the fuck out of our country. Go to whatever Middle Eastern nation has been paying your bills and go live there. Leave us the fuck alone. And it isn't just the influencers. The craziness is everywhere. I was on a right-wing show yesterday and suggested that Republicans lost because they've lost touch with reality. They spend too much time in their echo chambers and let crazy people run their campaigns, run for office, instead of qualified human beings who might actually know what the fuck they're doing. * A woman from Texas started screaming at me. James Talarico, she said, was going to steal my child and turn him trans. I hadn't even recovered from that when she explained the real reason Greg Abbott lost: he let too many Muslims into Texas. That's where the Republican Party is right now. In 2025 there were a million think pieces about whether Democrats would learn the lesson of 2024: that we were too often focused on the wrong things instead of passing legislation and focusing on ways to make a material difference in your life. That's the lesson Republicans should be learning right now. Instead, they're doubling down on the same stupid shit. Loomer crashing out about America becoming Islamic and a woman screaming about Muslims in Texas aren't outliers. They are the party. These people contribute nothing to society and nothing to public discourse except hate and lies. I hope someday they see the light and become more than the miserable human beings they are. I don't expect it. Here's where the fun of election night ends. As much they'll threaten to leave, they're not going anywhere. There's a presidential election coming, and it will be a huge opportunity to make money and steal influence. JD Vance is already rebuilding the freak coalition for 2028. He won't fully condemn Nick Fuentes, who is basically a white supremacist, and he's back-channeling with Tucker Carlson to keep him out of the race. They'll all make up and get back on the same page, because they hate Democrats, they hate liberal democracy, and they believe the American government is simply a piggy bank for corrupt billionaires like Donald Trump and Elon Musk, instead of the mechanism to improve your life. So yes, enjoy this week. You earned it! But these people will remain a corrosive force in American politics until they're removed from it, or at least marginalized to the point that they have no meaningful influence. Democrats aren't perfect. But, we have a real chance to show people what good government looks like, and part of that job is taking these people on and exposing exactly what they're doing. That doesn't happen on its own. When they lose, they whine on the internet. They threaten to leave. They blame Muslims and trans kids and anyone but themselves. When we lose, we go back to work the next morning. That's what I did in 2024, and it's what we'll keep doing until these people are gone from our politics. With urgency, --Mike Mike Nellis is a Democratic strategist and entrepreneur who has raised over $1 billion for Democratic campaigns and causes. He 's the founder of Authentic.org, an award-winning fundraising and advertising agency, and a former Senior Advisor to Vice President Kamala Harris. This Substack is where he writes with endless urgency about the issues of the day--and how we can save the Democratic Party and our democracy. | | Friend,

On Tuesday Oakland, Berkeley, Alameda, San Leandro, Piedmont, Emeryville, and Albany voted to send me back to Congress. I could not be more grateful.

And across the country, voters delivered a generational mandate for change.

We have our work cut out for us.

As the member of Congress for the East Bay, I can promise you this:

I will demand, and we will win affordability for our people. For the Oakland teachers who cannot afford a one-bedroom apartment, and for everyone struggling to make ends meet.

I will fight for healthcare for all – so that no child has to go without cancer treatment in the richest country on Earth.

I will fight with everything I have to dismantle Jim Crow 3.0 and end the attacks on Black life, and on the right to vote.

I will protect our neighbors who are immigrants, as well as our queer and trans community members.

I will demand that our taxpayer dollars never be used to buy bombs for Gaza, for Yemen, for Sudan, or for Haiti.

I will say no to illegal wars and I will vote for meals over munitions every single time.

I will spend my time chasing resources, not cameras – because I measure my success on the results that I deliver, rather than the headlines I generate.

**In the next Congress I will be even more determined, focused, and committed to the fight, because this moment requires it.**

So show up, hold me to every word, and call us out when we fail to deliver on the change that voters so clearly and desperately need.

I didn't get into politics because I enjoy shaking hands and raising money.

I ran for office to fight like hell for the people of the East Bay. God willing, that is what I am going back to do.

Thank you for your support, and I cannot wait to get back to work.

With hope,

Lateefah

# One last favor, and a big thank you
---
| | | | | | Friend,
I want to start with two words: thank you.
Thank you for the doors you knocked, the calls you made, the yard signs you put up, the events you showed up for, and every dollar you gave to this campaign. Whether you gave $5 or volunteered every weekend since spring, you were part of something that mattered.
The result wasn't what we worked for. But I'm proud of the campaign we ran and the ideas we put in front of New Mexicans: safer communities, a stronger economy, schools that deliver for our kids, and a state government that answers to the people it serves. Those ideas don't go away because an election is over. They're still worth fighting for, and I'll keep fighting for them.
I have one last favor to ask.
Our signs are still standing in yards, along roads, and on street corners across New Mexico. If you put one up, or you see one on property where you have permission, please take it down this week and either recycle it or throw it away. Please don't remove signs from private property without the owner's okay, and stay safe near traffic.
Leaving our communities cleaner than we found them is the right way to close out this campaign.
Being your candidate has been one of the great honors of my life. Carrie and I are grateful to every one of you.
With gratitude,

subject: What’s next for Drop Site
body:
The newsletters that run Capitol Hill are written for insiders. Ours won't be.

| |
---|---|---
|
# What's next for Drop Site
### The newsletters that run Capitol Hill are written for insiders. Ours won't be.
| | | [Ryan Grim](https://substack.com/@ryangrim)
---
| Nov 5
---
| [](https://substack.com/@ryangrim)
---
At Drop Site, [we're launching something new that we need your help with](https://substack.com/redirect/064bac69-eb30-4607-8e3e-c53975464461?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). More on how you can help below, but first, let me lay out the problem we plan to solve.
### **What voters asked for**
Look at what even JD Vance said out loud after the election. In his own words, he interpreted the results of Tuesday's election as an order from the voters to:
1. End the war
2. Focus on cost of living/inflation
3. Put America First
4. Change our relationship to Israel

Democrats, broadly, agree with that set of priorities, particularly the new candidates who won this week. So the agenda of Congress, and the approach to covering it by the media, obviously ought to reflect this new mandate, right? If only it was that easy.
### **What the coverage left out**
CNN's first impulse, for instance, was to ask James Talarico - apparently in all sincerity - if he will stand up to Abdul El-Sayed in the Senate. And as votes were being cast on Tuesday, Punchbowl, which runs a powerful and widely read Capitol Hill newsletter, reported in a text message, exclusively to subscribers: "Top House and Senate Republican and Democratic appropriators are planning to meet early next week to discuss FY2027 funding. Gov. funding runs out on Dec. 11. This four corners meeting will kick off lame-duck spending talks."
You might notice something about that news report: **It is utterly inscrutable to anybody who isn 't steeped in Capitol Hill minutiae**. What funding choices will be discussed? What are the battle lines? What on earth is a "four corners meeting" and is this something the public can participate in - since, after all, they will be spending the people's money on, allegedly, the voters' priorities.
If the goal of the news item was to mystify the process and keep the public out of it, mission accomplished.
What the news item left out is crucial, however: The December 11th deadline is an opportunity for Democrats and antiwar Republicans to cut off money for the war in a way that would genuinely force it to end, just as Vice President J.D. Vance says we ought to. That's how the Vietnam war was brought to an end by Congress, and that's how this one can be.
Yet top-ranking Democrats and Republicans are working quickly and quietly behind the scenes to pass a spending bill that makes it impossible to have that fight, leaving the war-making power in the hands of President Trump. Sounds like big news, right?
That's the news people need to know, so they can act on it before it's too late, and before we're back in another phase of the war voters so fiercely rejected.

### **Who Capitol Hill news is written for**
The structure of today's congressional reporting is such that it can't truly produce the kind of journalism the public needs to be able to weigh in. The audience is lobbyists and insiders, and the advertisers are the ones most heavily affected by Congress: defense contractors, AI, Big Pharma, financial institutions and crypto, and Big Oil make up the bulk of the revenue for the media companies covering Capitol Hill.
The dominant forces are Punchbowl, Politico, and Axios, each of which publish influential newsletters. But when it comes to issues of war and peace, AI, or Israel, their coverage routinely pulls punches.
Capitol Hill's information ecosystem is heavily contaminated by newsletter culture, but there isn't a single newsletter that is aimed at a mass public audience. The thinking is that the public just doesn't care enough. But there used to be one in the 2010s. It was called HuffPost Hill, and in its prime it had a huge readership and was highly influential on the Hill. Everyone read it because everyone read it, and it broke news that the others would miss. In January, ten or eleven new Democratic senators will arrive in town, joined by many dozens of House freshmen. If it's simply the toxic corporate brew that's served up today, we shouldn't be surprised at what comes out the other end.

We need millions of people reading this newsletter who can then produce social media content based on it, which'll give the public the chance to weigh in on congressional action.
### **The December fights**
It doesn't just start in January. In December there will be major votes on Senate majority leader, the war funding measure, and perhaps the National Defense Authorization Act, which pro-Israel forces are trying to use to fuse the Israeli and U.S. military industrial bases.

Friend,
---
| | | Her name is Luka Hein. She was **16 years old** when doctors removed her breasts. **Now she wants a jury to hear what happened to her.** But getting Luka into that courtroom has become a battle of its own. I’m Mark Trammell, CEO of the**Center for American Liberty** , a nonprofit public interest law firm that takes on cases many organizations won’t touch. And I’m asking you to help us fight for Luka.
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
[ **Help Luka Get Her Day in Court** ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
As we described in her lawsuit, Luka was a deeply troubled teenager. Her parents had divorced. She struggled with anxiety, isolation, school, panic attacks, self-harm, and thoughts of suicide. Then she encountered transgender influencers online. At 15, Luka began receiving gender-related care. At 16, doctors removed her breasts. Testosterone came months later. Luka now alleges that the medical professionals who treated her failed to provide the proper standard of care and failed to obtain informed consent. **Her case is headed toward a jury trial currently scheduled for June, 2027.** **But the legal battle is already raging.** Right now, the defendants are challenging expert testimony Luka intends to present regarding the standard of care. **These kinds of fights mean more motions, more legal work, more time, and more expense.**
---
[ **Help Luka Get Her Day in Court** ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
And that can become a strategy all its own — **make litigation so long and expensive that the other side runs out of resources.** **We refuse to let that happen.** We’ve been here before. The **Center for American Liberty** represents detransitioner **Chloe Cole** in her lawsuit against the medical providers she alleged harmed her. The hospital defendants aggressively filed motions delaying Chloe’s trial by years. We fought back and now Chloe’s trial is scheduled for April. **We are prepared to fight just as hard for Luka.** But unlike the powerful institutions we face, the **Center for American Liberty** is a nonprofit. **We depend on Americans like you.** **[Your first gift of $25, $50, $100, $250, or whatever you can give, helps us answer these legal challenges and keep Luka’s case moving toward a jury.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)**
---
[ **Help Luka Get Her Day in Court** ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
**This is why our organization exists.** There are Americans all across this country who have been silenced, pushed out, or left to fight powerful institutions alone. We stand beside them. **And we fight.** I came to the **Center for American Liberty** because I wanted to get my hands dirty and be in the courtroom fighting these cases because somebody has to do it. As I often ask: **Who’s going to represent these people if we don’t?** Luka had the courage to put her name on this lawsuit. She is prepared to tell a jury what happened. Now she needs Americans willing to stand behind her. Please make your first gift to the **Center for American Liberty** today. Help us fight every legal obstacle between Luka and her day in court. For Liberty,
---
| | | Mark Trammell
Chief Executive Officer
Center for American Liberty
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
**P.S.** Powerful institutions can spend enormous sums defending themselves. **Your first gift today helps make sure Luka doesn’t have to fight them alone**. Please stand with her now. Donate today.
---
[ **Support Center For American Liberty** ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---

Derek –

I wanted you to get this update from me:
Ballots are still being counted, and right now, it’s still too close to
call.

We are going to do everything we can to make sure every single vote is
counted in this race.

But I’ll be honest: That is going to take time – and plenty of resources
that we don’t currently have.

As we fight to make sure every ballot is counted, we’re going to remain
the top target of the DC establishment.

We put everything we had into winning this race, so I’m counting on your
help to fight back against their attacks.

It looks like we’re in this for the long haul, so I need your help to

From the very beginning, this campaign has been powered by grassroots

subject: With deepest gratitude
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Clark for Wisconsin Clark for Wisconsin
body:

Friend, The results are in, and our race for the 7th Congressional District was called in favor of Michael Alfonso. I called Michael on Election Night and congratulated him.

I’m disappointed, of course, and I know that disappointment is shared by our team and so many of our enthusiastic supporters. And on behalf of our team I want to extend our sincere gratitude to the hundreds of people who have helped us run this campaign.

**It’s worth looking at the big picture to see how far we’ve come. For a seat won by a 26% margin in 2024, we cut that margin by more than half to 12%. **

We launched this campaign knowing we wouldn’t have millions to spend and knowing we’d have to earn every dollar and every vote. We worked hard, we looked out for all our neighbors, and we ran a campaign that showed respect for everyone.

And we’ve already accomplished some things that all that Washington and corporate money could never buy. We built a stronger and broader coalition than we have seen in many years here in Northern Wisconsin. And that coalition lives on, and that’s only going to get stronger.

We can be proud that our efforts helped contribute to strong Democratic majorities in Congress and in Madison.

**I’m asking all our supporters today to make a promise: Let’s hold elected officials of all parties in Washington and in Madison accountable for a government that’s constitutional, fair, and moral. **

And let’s rest up and go back tomorrow, or the next day, to the work of being citizens and members of an incredible community.

Along with so many of you, we’ve created a movement and it’s bigger than me or any one of us, and it will last as long as we continue to invest in this work together.

_“You are not obligated to complete the work, but neither are you free to abandon it.” — _The Talmud

On behalf of our entire team, I want to extend our warmest and most sincere thanks to everyone who has supported our campaign in so many different ways. Together we _have_ made a difference.

With deepest gratitude,
Fred

clean_body: Everything we worked for comes down to this moment. | Fellow American, I know our team has asked for your help all cycle long. You’ve read the emails, you’ve seen the updates from the road, and you’ve stood with me through months of hard campaigning. I wouldn't be reaching out right now if this wasn’t the most critical moment of my entire time serving you: I am ready to stand my ground and defend every lawful vote. But entering into these intense legal battles across the state takes an ballot reviews, answering every challenge, and keeping legal teams working around the clock We need all the help we can get right now. If you have already given this cycle, thank you from the bottom of my heart. I'll be honest with you. I'm frustrated with how the 2026 midterms turned out, and if you're reading this, I'd guess you are too.Look at what we watched happen this cycle. On Election Day, ballot scanners failed across Westchester County, **New York** , in one of the closest House races in the country, held by a Republican incumbent, and poll workers stuffed completed ballots into emergency bags saying they would just be counted later. In **California** , federal officials flagged roughly 20,000 likely non-citizens who had been mailed ballots, and an appeals court let the state count them anyway.**New Jersey** admitted it found 6,600 non-citizens on its own voter rolls. And in one **California** county, election staff opened a locked drop box and found nearly 600 sealed ballots that had sat there uncounted for five months after the election was certified.On top of all that, the Supreme Court ruled this summer that 14 states and D.C. can keep counting mail ballots that arrive after Election Day. **_Election Day is supposed to mean one day._** After a night like this, it's tempting to tune out and wait for things to cool down. I _understand that feeling._ But these problems don't fix themselves between elections. First and foremost, I want to thank you.
To everyone who donated, volunteered, posted, shared a kind word about me or the importance of this election with friends or family members... Thank you.
Together, in this election, we did the most American thing possible: We took power into our own hands and we did it at the ballot box.
We kept faith with the idea that we're a government of the people, by the people, for the people.
We sent a message to Trump and his friends in the Epstein class, to the oligarchs, to the robber barons, to the corrupt: your time in power is ending.
We did it in my district in western Pennsylvania, we did it across the entire commonwealth, and we did it across the country.
So what happens next?
It doesn't need to be complicated.
We must end the war in Iran.
And we must ensure that the people of this country who work hard, bust their butt, and play by the rules have a shot at a decent life.
That if you do those things, you have a roof over your head, living where you want to and being able to do it with one job. That you get to start a family when you want and be able to spend time with your newborn child after they are born. That you get to go to the doctor when you need to and can get the medicine you need to live a healthy life without going bankrupt.
Not complicated. Not radical.
Not easy, either.
Because while we won an election — that is not the end point, it is simply a checkpoint in a larger journey. A necessary one... but not the final one.
So thank you for your support and everything you did to make Tuesday possible. And I look forward to taking the next steps together in the future.
Don't give up the ship,
Chris Deluzio

| | Dear Team Maxine, **Tuesday was an incredible night.** I am deeply grateful to the people of Oregon's 3rd Congressional District for placing their trust in me to continue representing them in Congress. It is an incredible honor to serve this community, and I don't take that responsibility lightly. The results of this election were beyond our wildest imagination. Up against hundreds of millions of dollars from billionaires and corporate interests, we saw the extraordinary power of people coming together. No amount of money could silence the volunteers knocking on doors, the neighbors organizing their communities, or the people who showed up for one another and refused to give up. **This victory belongs to you.** I first ran for Congress because, as a physician, I know that the health, safety, and resilience of our communities depend on elected leaders who put people ahead of corporations and special interests. Over the past two years, I've brought that commitment to Congress, fighting to lower costs, protect access to healthcare, defend our fundamental freedoms, and hold those in power accountable. From standing up for our immigrant neighbors and protecting our environment to delivering meaningful results for veterans and working families, I'm proud of what we've accomplished.
---
| | |
---
| |
---
| |
---
| |
---
| | | **And we're just getting started.** The promise of America has never been about where we come from. It's about what we can build together and the future we choose to create. When we show up for one another, we demonstrate what we stand for: dignity, compassion, community, and the belief that our greatest strength comes from one another. **Elections matter. Showing up matters. And what we do next matters just as much.** To everyone who knocked on doors, donated, volunteered, shared our message, encouraged a neighbor, or simply believed in what we're working toward: **thank you. You made this possible.** As we look toward the next Congress, my commitment remains the same: to listen, lead with compassion, fight for the people I represent, and work every day to build a future where everyone has the opportunity to thrive. I'm energized by what's ahead, and I'm grateful to have you alongside me. Now, let's get to work. **❤️** With gratitude,Maxine

clean_body: | | | | | Dear Team Maxine, Tuesday was an incredible night. I am deeply grateful to the people of Oregon's 3rd Congressional District for placing their trust in me to continue representing them in Congress. It is an incredible honor to serve this community, and I don't take that responsibility lightly. The results of this election were beyond our wildest imagination. Up against hundreds of millions of dollars from billionaires and corporate interests, we saw the extraordinary power of people coming together. No amount of money could silence the volunteers knocking on doors, the neighbors organizing their communities, or the people who showed up for one another and refused to give up. This victory belongs to you. I first ran for Congress because, as a physician, I know that the health, safety, and resilience of our communities depend on elected leaders who put people ahead of corporations and special interests. Over the past two years, I've brought that commitment to Congress, fighting to lower costs, protect access to healthcare, defend our fundamental freedoms, and hold those in power accountable. From standing up for our immigrant neighbors and protecting our environment to delivering meaningful results for veterans and working families, I'm proud of what we've accomplished. | | | | | | | | | | | | And we're just getting started. The promise of America has never been about where we come from. It's about what we can build together and the future we choose to create. When we show up for one another, we demonstrate what we stand for: dignity, compassion, community, and the belief that our greatest strength comes from one another. Elections matter. Showing up matters. And what we do next matters just as much. To everyone who knocked on doors, donated, volunteered, shared our message, encouraged a neighbor, or simply believed in what we're working toward: thank you. You made this possible. As we look toward the next Congress, my commitment remains the same: to listen, lead with compassion, fight for the people I represent, and work every day to build a future where everyone has the opportunity to thrive. I'm energized by what's ahead, and I'm grateful to have you alongside me. Now, let's get to work. ❤️ With gratitude,Maxine = | | | | | | | Maxine Dexter is a critical care physician with decades of experience using facts and following science to help her patients. Now she's using those skills in Congress to ensure healthy communities by standing up to Big Pharma, fighting climate change, and expanding reproductive rights, as well as rebuilding a fair economy for all by protecting Social Security and Medicare.
